subjects.name: Musik
subjects.description: Compulsory subject from Klasse 1, regulated by the Länder (no KMK Bildungsstandards; the Abitur follows the KMK EPA Musik of 2005). At the Gymnasium, Klasse 7–10 combine music theory, music history by Epochen, popular music, jazz and class music-making, usually 1–2 lessons a week (in some Länder not in every year). In the Oberstufe Musik is a course with grundlegendem or erhöhtem Anforderungsniveau (Grund-/Leistungskurs) and an Abitur subject built on analysis, history and aesthetics, with practical parts in some Länder. Programmes such as JeKits (NRW) and Bläser- or Streicherklassen add instrumental tuition in the lower years.

subjects.name: Kunst
subjects.description: Compulsory subject from Klasse 1 (often 'Kunst' or 'Bildende Kunst'), regulated by the Länder (no KMK Bildungsstandards; the Abitur follows the KMK EPA Kunst of 2005). Gymnasium Klasse 7–10 deepen drawing, painting, sculpture, printmaking, design, photography and film and add Bildanalyse and Kunstgeschichte (chronological in Bayern, thematic in NRW and Berlin-Brandenburg). In the Oberstufe Kunst is a Grund- or Leistungskurs (gA/eA) and an Abitur subject that combines bildnerische Praxis with Werkanalyse and interpretation.

subjects.name: Sport
subjects.description: Compulsory subject from Klasse 1 to the Abitur, usually three lessons a week, organised by Bewegungsfelder and pedagogical perspectives and regulated by the Länder (no KMK Bildungsstandards; for Sport as an Abitur subject the KMK EPA Sport of 2005, amended 2017, apply). School swimming aims at sicheres Schwimmen (Bronze) by the end of the Grundschule and continues with Silber/Gold and Rettungsschwimmen; the Bundesjugendspiele are held every year. In the Oberstufe Sport can be an Abitur subject with a practical exam and sport theory (Trainingslehre, Bewegungslehre, Sport und Gesellschaft), as a Leistungskurs or eA course in several Länder.

subjects.name: Religion & Ethik
subjects.description: Religionsunterricht is an ordinary, confessionally bound subject (Art. 7 Abs. 3 GG: evangelisch, katholisch, increasingly islamisch, also jüdisch, alevitisch, orthodox). Pupils who opt out attend an Ersatzfach: Ethik (most Länder), Praktische Philosophie (NRW Sek I), Werte und Normen (Niedersachsen) or LER (Brandenburg, ordinary subject Kl. 5–10). Berlin has compulsory Ethik in Kl. 7–10, and Philosophie is the usual Oberstufe subject in many Länder. Ethik, Philosophie and ev./kath. Religionslehre are Abitur subjects (KMK EPA 2006). This taxonomy models the content these classes share: values and philosophical inquiry in the lower years; ethical theories, applied ethics, anthropology, epistemology, philosophy of mind, state and justice, religions and religion and science from Klasse 7 to the Abitur. Confession-specific variants are noted per topic.

topics.subject: Musik
topics.name: Naming and Hearing Intervals
topics.nameDe: Intervalle bestimmen und hören (Prime bis Oktave)
topics.description: Name intervals from the unison to the octave by counting steps and semitones (kleine/große Terz, reine Quinte …), write them on the staff and recognise characteristic ones by ear. Intervals are the building block for scales, chords and harmony.
evidence: Name the size and quality of intervals up to the octave written on the staff (e.g. große Terz, reine Quarte)
Write a given interval above or below a note, including accidentals
Recognise by ear at least the octave, fifth, major and minor third in short examples
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees C–E and C–E♭ on the staff, can they name both intervals and sing or play the difference?

prerequisites.reason: Intervals are measured in whole and half steps of the scale
Counting intervals needs secure reading of notes on the staff

topics.laenderNotes: Some Länder (e.g. Bayern) start interval work in Kl. 5–6; Berlin-Brandenburg lists intervals among the possible contents for Kl. 7–10.

topics.subject: Musik
topics.name: Major and Minor Keys
topics.nameDe: Dur- und Molltonleitern, parallele Tonarten
topics.description: Build major and natural minor scales on any note from the pattern of whole and half steps, find the key of a melody from its key signature and final note, and relate each major key to its relative minor (Paralleltonart) a minor third below.
evidence: Write a major and a natural minor scale on a given note with correct accidentals
Name the relative minor of a major key and explain why they share a key signature
Decide whether a short melody is in major or minor from its sound and last note
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} gets a melody in A minor without sharps or flats, can they explain why it is not in C major?

prerequisites.reason: Builds directly on the whole/half-step structure of the scale
The relative minor lies a minor third below the major key

topics.subject: Musik
topics.name: The Circle of Fifths
topics.nameDe: Quintenzirkel
topics.description: Use the circle of fifths to find the key signature of any major or minor key, see how each step adds a sharp or flat, and identify closely related keys. It is the standard classroom tool for Tonartenbestimmung.
evidence: Draw the circle of fifths with major keys and their relative minors
State the number and order of sharps or flats for a named key
Name the neighbouring keys of a key on the circle and explain why they are closely related
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} is asked for the key signature of E major, can they work it out with the circle of fifths?

prerequisites.reason: The circle orders the major and minor keys
Neighbouring keys are a perfect fifth apart

topics.subject: Musik
topics.name: Triads and Inversions
topics.nameDe: Dreiklänge (Dur, Moll, vermindert, übermäßig) und Umkehrungen
topics.description: Build triads by stacking thirds, tell major, minor, diminished and augmented triads apart on paper and by ear, and recognise root position, first and second inversion (Sextakkord, Quartsextakkord).
evidence: Build major and minor triads on any note and name their thirds
Identify a written triad as major, minor, diminished or augmented
Recognise and write the inversions of a triad
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees the notes E–G–C, can they say which triad it is and in which position?

prerequisites.reason: Triads are stacks of major and minor thirds
Triad qualities follow from the scale degrees of a key

topics.subject: Musik
topics.name: Primary Chords and the Cadence
topics.nameDe: Hauptstufen und Kadenz: Tonika, Subdominante, Dominante
topics.description: Identify chords I, IV and V of a key as Tonika, Subdominante and Dominante, hear the tension and release of the cadence T–S–D–T, add the dominant seventh chord, and label chords with function symbols and pop chord symbols.
evidence: Play or write T, S, D and D7 in a given major key
Label the chords of a simple song with function symbols or chord symbols
Tell by ear whether a phrase ends with a full close (Ganzschluss) or a half close (Halbschluss)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} plays C, F, G7 and C, can they explain which chord creates the tension and why the last chord sounds like an ending?

prerequisites.reason: The cadence is built from triads on degrees I, IV and V
Chord functions are defined relative to a key

topics.laenderNotes: Function theory (Funktionstheorie, T–S–D) is the usual German way of naming chords; step numbers (I–IV–V) and pop chord symbols are taught alongside, depending on Land and textbook.

topics.subject: Musik
topics.name: Bass Clef and Score Reading
topics.nameDe: Bassschlüssel und Partiturlesen
topics.description: Read notes in the bass clef, follow a part in an orchestral or band score while listening (Mitlesen), and understand score layout: order of instrument groups, braces, transposing instruments and common performance markings.
evidence: Name notes in the bass clef across two octaves
Follow one instrument through a printed score while the recording plays and point to the current bar
Explain the order of instrument groups in an orchestral score
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} listens to a symphony excerpt with the score, can they show where the cellos have the melody?

prerequisites.reason: Reading the treble clef comes first
Score order follows the instrument families

topics.subject: Musik
topics.name: Syncopation, Off-Beat and Swing
topics.nameDe: Synkope, Off-Beat und binäre/ternäre Spielweise
topics.description: Perform and notate syncopations and off-beat accents, feel the backbeat in rock and pop, and tell straight (binär) from swung (ternär) eighth notes, including the gap between notation and performance practice in popular music.
evidence: Clap or play a notated syncopated rhythm against a steady beat
Mark the syncopations in the score of a pop song
Play the same eighth-note line straight and swung and describe the difference
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} hears a pop song with a strong backbeat, can they clap the off-beat and then write down a syncopated rhythm from the chorus?

prerequisites.reason: Syncopation is defined against the metre
Notating syncopations needs ties and dotted values

topics.subject: Musik
topics.name: Musical Acoustics and Overtones
topics.nameDe: Akustische Grundlagen: Frequenz, Obertöne, Klangfarbe
topics.description: Explain musical sound physically: pitch as frequency, loudness as amplitude and timbre as the mix of overtones (Naturtonreihe). Relate the overtone series to brass instruments and to octave and fifth, and connect sound levels to protecting one's hearing.
evidence: Relate higher pitch to higher frequency and an octave to a doubled frequency
Explain with a spectrum or sound picture why a flute and a violin playing the same note sound different
Show how a brass player gets different natural notes without valves
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} hears a trumpet and a clarinet play the same note, can they explain why the two still sound different?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on the Kl. 6 science topic on how sound arises, pitch and loudness
Instrument examples illustrate overtone spectra

externalPrerequisites.subject: Physik
externalPrerequisites.concept: acoustics: sound waves, frequency, amplitude and resonance
externalPrerequisites.reason: The physics lesson supplies the wave model used here

topics.laenderNotes: In Bayern the overtone series is Musisches-Gymnasium content in Kl. 8; Physik usually treats acoustics in Kl. 7–8 as well.

topics.subject: Musik
topics.name: The Voice and Voice Change
topics.nameDe: Stimme, Stimmwechsel (Mutation), Stimmlagen und Register
topics.description: Understand how the voice works (breath, vocal folds, resonance), what happens during voice change in puberty, which voice types and registers exist and how to sing healthily, and use the changing voice creatively, e.g. in rap or rhythmic speech.
evidence: Describe the roles of breathing, vocal folds and resonance in a sung tone
Explain how voices change in puberty and how to sing safely during the change
Name soprano, alto, tenor and bass and find their own current range
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}}'s voice is breaking, can they explain what is happening and choose a comfortable part or a rap part instead of straining?

prerequisites.reason: Part-singing gave experience with different voice parts
The science topic on puberty explains the bodily changes

topics.subject: Musik
topics.name: Singing in Multi-Part Arrangements
topics.nameDe: Mehrstimmige Arrangements singen (Chorsatz, Popsong)
topics.description: Hold an independent part in a three- or four-part vocal arrangement (choir piece or pop song), tune to the other voices, follow a conductor and shape dynamics and phrasing together.
evidence: Sing their own part securely while other parts sound
Read their part from a choral score and find their entries
Adjust volume and intonation to blend with the group
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}}'s class rehearses a three-part arrangement, can they keep their part when the other voices come in?

prerequisites.reason: Rounds and two-part songs are the first step to part-singing
Knowing one's voice type helps to choose a part

topics.subject: Musik
topics.name: Playing in the Class Band
topics.nameDe: Klassenmusizieren mit Bandinstrumenten: Groove und Akkordbegleitung
topics.description: Play a rock or pop song in a class band on keyboard, guitar, bass, drums or percussion: keep a groove, change chords from chord symbols (e.g. I–V–vi–IV) and follow the song form.
evidence: Play a simple drum groove or bass line in time with the group
Change between at least three chords on keyboard or guitar from chord symbols
Follow the form (intro, verse, chorus) and come in at the right place
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}}'s class plays a pop song, can they keep their part going through verse and chorus without stopping when the chords change?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on ensemble playing in Kl. 5–6
Chord changes follow the cadence and chord symbols

topics.subject: Musik
topics.name: Performing a Prepared Piece in Style
topics.nameDe: Stilgerechter Vortrag eines einstudierten Werkes
topics.description: Rehearse a piece from a chosen era independently, perform it vocally or instrumentally with a personal interpretation, and justify interpretive choices with knowledge of style and structure. This is the practical part of the Musik Abitur in Länder that test it.
evidence: Prepare and perform a piece with secure notes, rhythm and expression
Explain how their tempo, dynamics and articulation fit the style of the era
Demonstrate a passage vocally or instrumentally to illustrate an analysis
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} performs a Baroque piece in the practical exam, can they explain why they chose a light articulation and terraced dynamics?

prerequisites.reason: Rehearsal and performance routines from Kl. 1–6
Ensemble experience supports performing
Interpretive choices need criteria

topics.laenderNotes: Practical exam parts (musikpraktische Prüfung) exist only in some Länder; others examine Musik in writing or orally without a performance.

topics.subject: Musik
topics.name: Motif, Theme and Variation
topics.nameDe: Motiv, Thema, Motivverarbeitung und Variation
topics.description: Identify a motif and a theme in a piece, follow how composers develop them (repetition, sequence, inversion, augmentation, fragmentation) and how a theme is varied in rhythm, harmony or character.
evidence: Point out the main motif of a well-known piece and where it returns
Name at least three techniques of motivic development in a listening example or score
Describe how a variation differs from its theme
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} hears the opening of Beethoven's Fifth Symphony, can they show how the four-note motif keeps coming back in changed forms?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on recognising repetition and contrast
Inversion and sequence are described with intervals

topics.subject: Musik
topics.name: Film Music: Functions and Techniques
topics.nameDe: Filmmusik: Funktionen und Techniken (Paraphrasierung, Kontrapunktierung, Leitmotiv)
topics.description: Analyse how film music works: underscoring, paraphrasing (Paraphrasierung), polarising and counterpointing (Kontrapunktierung), leitmotifs, diegetic and non-diegetic music, mickey-mousing, and how music steers the viewer's emotions.
evidence: Name the function of the music in a film scene, e.g. paraphrasing or counterpointing
Identify a leitmotif and explain which character or idea it stands for
Put different music under a short clip and describe how the effect of the scene changes
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} watches a scene twice with different music, can they explain with technical terms how the music changes what we feel?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on describing mood and effect of music
Programme music already links music to stories

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern: Kl. 8; Berlin-Brandenburg lists film music under 'Funktionale Musik' for Kl. 7–10; it often returns in the Oberstufe under music and media.

topics.subject: Musik
topics.name: Word and Music in Song
topics.nameDe: Wort-Ton-Verhältnis in Lied und Song
topics.description: Examine how composers set words to music: syllabic and melismatic setting, word painting, rhythm following the speech stresses, and strophic versus through-composed form, in art songs (Kunstlied) and pop songs alike.
evidence: Find examples of word painting in a song and explain them
Tell a strophic from a through-composed song and explain the choice
Describe how melody and rhythm follow the stresses of the text
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} listens to Schubert's 'Erlkönig', can they show how the music tells narrator, father, child and Erlkönig apart?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on describing the effect of music
Understanding imagery in poems shows what the music depicts

externalPrerequisites.subject: Deutsch
externalPrerequisites.concept: analysing poems: metre, rhyme and imagery
externalPrerequisites.reason: Lyrics are analysed with the tools of poetry analysis

topics.subject: Musik
topics.name: Sonata Form
topics.nameDe: Sonatenhauptsatzform: Exposition, Durchführung, Reprise
topics.description: Follow the sections of sonata form (exposition with two contrasting themes and key areas, development, recapitulation, coda) by ear and in the score, and explain how the form builds drama through contrast and return.
evidence: Draw a form diagram of a sonata movement with themes and keys
Identify the start of the development and the recapitulation by ear
Explain how the second theme's key changes between exposition and recapitulation
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} listens to the first movement of a Mozart symphony, can they say when the development begins and what happens to the themes there?

prerequisites.reason: The development works with motifs and themes
Key areas are heard through dominant tension
Themes move to related keys

topics.subject: Musik
topics.name: Opera and Musical
topics.nameDe: Oper und Musical: Rezitativ, Arie, Ensemble, Song
topics.description: Compare the forms of music theatre: recitative and aria, ensemble and chorus in opera, song and dance numbers in the musical. Analyse how music characterises figures and drives the drama, e.g. in Mozart or in Bernstein's 'West Side Story'.
evidence: Tell a recitative from an aria and explain their dramatic functions
Describe how the music characterises two figures in one scene
Compare an opera and a musical in form, use of voice and audience
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} watches a scene from 'West Side Story', can they explain how the music shows the conflict between the two gangs?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on children's opera, ballet and musical in Kl. 3–6
Word setting explains how characters are drawn

topics.subject: Musik
topics.name: Polyphony and Fugue
topics.nameDe: Polyphonie und Fuge
topics.description: Distinguish homophonic and polyphonic textures and follow the structure of a fugue (subject, answer, countersubject, exposition, episodes, stretto), mainly in the music of Johann Sebastian Bach.
evidence: Describe a passage as homophonic or polyphonic and justify it
Mark the entries of the subject in a short fugue score
Explain subject, answer and episode with an example
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} hears a Bach fugue, can they count the voices as they enter with the subject?

prerequisites.reason: Rounds are the simplest imitative polyphony
A fugue subject is developed like a motif

topics.subject: Musik
topics.name: Methods of Music Analysis
topics.nameDe: Methoden der Werkanalyse: Hören, Notentext, Formübersicht
topics.description: Analyse a longer work systematically: listen with and without the score, describe the parameters (melody, harmony, rhythm, texture, instrumentation, form) in technical language with bar references, draw form charts, and combine the findings into an interpretation. This is the core of the written Abitur task 'Untersuchung, Analyse und Interpretation'.
evidence: Write a structured analysis of an excerpt covering several parameters with bar references
Draw a form chart or listening protocol of a movement
Link analytical findings to an interpretation of the work's meaning or effect
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} gets an unknown score excerpt in the Abitur, can they describe its structure with bar numbers and explain what the composer achieves?

prerequisites.reason: Analysis needs secure score reading
Knowledge of standard forms frames the analysis
Analysis ends in a reasoned judgement

externalPrerequisites.subject: Deutsch
externalPrerequisites.concept: writing a structured analytical essay with evidence
externalPrerequisites.reason: The written analysis follows the conventions of an analytical text

topics.subject: Musik
topics.name: Songwriting
topics.nameDe: Songwriting: Text vertonen, Melodie und Akkordfolge
topics.description: Write a short song: choose or write lyrics, set them to a melody that follows the speech rhythm, build verse and chorus over a chord progression, and notate or record the result.
evidence: Write a verse and chorus with a singable melody that fits the text stresses
Put the melody over a chord progression and write the chord symbols
Present the song and explain one musical decision
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} writes a chorus about a school topic, can they make the important words fall on strong beats and put fitting chords under it?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on composing with rhythm building blocks in Kl. 5–6
The progression uses the primary chords

topics.subject: Musik
topics.name: Producing Music with a DAW
topics.nameDe: Musikproduktion mit DAW: Aufnahme, Loops, Effekte
topics.description: Use a digital audio workstation or music app to record, arrange loops and samples, edit (cut, quantise, mix) and add effects, producing a short track or remix and documenting the steps.
evidence: Record or import audio and MIDI tracks and arrange them on a timeline
Use quantising, volume and panning and at least one effect deliberately
Export a finished track and explain how it was built
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} is asked to make a 30-second jingle on a tablet, can they layer drums, bass and melody and balance the mix?

prerequisites.reason: Songwriting provides material to produce
Effects and mixing change sound properties
Builds on responsible media use

externalPrerequisites.subject: Informatik & Medienbildung
externalPrerequisites.concept: digitising sound: sampling rate, bit depth and audio file formats
externalPrerequisites.reason: Explains what audio files contain

topics.subject: Musik
topics.name: Improvising over the Blues
topics.nameDe: Improvisation über das Bluesschema
topics.description: Improvise short melodic phrases over a 12-bar blues with the blues scale, call-and-response and motifs, keeping the form and the swing feel.
evidence: Play the 12-bar blues progression or follow it while others play
Improvise two- and four-bar phrases with the blues scale
Answer a phrase played by someone else (call and response)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}}'s class jams a 12-bar blues, can they take a four-bar solo with the blues scale and come back in on time?

prerequisites.reason: The blues form and scale come from jazz
Builds on call-and-response improvising
Swing phrasing and syncopation

topics.subject: Musik
topics.name: Arranging for the Class Ensemble
topics.nameDe: Arrangieren für das Klassenensemble
topics.description: Arrange a melody or song for the class instruments: choose a texture (melody with accompaniment, bass line, rhythm), write parts within each instrument's range, and test and revise the arrangement in rehearsal.
evidence: Write an accompaniment pattern and bass line for a given melody
Give the parts to instruments with suitable ranges
Rehearse the arrangement and revise a passage that did not work
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} gets a simple tune, can they write parts for keyboard, bass and percussion that the class can play?

prerequisites.reason: Playing in the band shows which parts are needed
Parts are written as a score

topics.subject: Musik
topics.name: Composing to a Brief with Commentary
topics.nameDe: Gestaltungsaufgabe mit schriftlicher Erläuterung
topics.description: Compose or arrange music to set requirements (e.g. variations on a theme, a song setting, a piece in a given style) and explain and justify the compositional means in writing, an Abitur task type in Musik.
evidence: Compose a short piece that meets all given requirements
Explain in writing which musical means they used and why
Evaluate the result against the brief and suggest an improvement
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} has to set a short poem in Romantic style, can they compose it and explain their harmonic choices in writing?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on arranging
Harmonic choices draw on extended harmony

topics.subject: Musik
topics.name: Four-Part Choral Writing
topics.nameDe: Vierstimmiger Chorsatz
topics.description: Arrange a melody with chord symbols or figured bass for mixed choir (SATB) following voice-leading rules: ranges, no parallel fifths or octaves, resolution of leading notes and sevenths.
evidence: Write a four-part harmonisation of a short melody
Check the setting for parallel fifths and octaves and correct them
Resolve the leading note and the dominant seventh correctly
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} harmonises a chorale phrase for SATB, can they avoid parallel fifths and lead the leading note upwards?

prerequisites.reason: Voice leading needs secure harmony
Singing in parts shows how voices move

topics.laenderNotes: Choral arranging is eA content in Bayern (Mu12); in other Länder Tonsatz exercises appear in the Leistungskurs or not at all.

topics.subject: Musik
topics.name: Extended Harmony
topics.nameDe: Erweiterte Harmonik: Nebenstufen, Septakkorde, Zwischendominante, Modulation
topics.description: Analyse harmony beyond the primary chords: secondary chords (Nebenstufen, Parallelen), seventh and diminished chords, secondary dominants and modulation to related keys, with function or step symbols.
evidence: Label the chords of a short chorale or song including secondary chords
Find a secondary dominant and the chord it resolves to
Show where and how a piece modulates
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} analyses a Bach chorale, can they spot the secondary dominant before the half close and name the new key?

prerequisites.reason: Extends the primary-chord cadence
Modulation moves to related keys on the circle

topics.laenderNotes: At the Musisches Gymnasium in Bayern secondary dominants and modulation come in Kl. 9.

topics.subject: Musik
topics.name: History of Popular Music and Youth Cultures
topics.nameDe: Geschichte der Popularmusik und Jugendkulturen
topics.description: Trace the main styles of popular music from blues and rock 'n' roll via beat, punk and disco to hip-hop and electronic music, relate them to youth cultures and social change, and name their musical features (instrumentation, rhythm, sound).
evidence: Place five popular music styles on a timeline with one example each
Describe the typical instrumentation and rhythm of two styles
Explain how one style expressed the attitude of a youth culture
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} hears a punk song and a disco song, can they describe the differences and name the youth cultures linked to them?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on reflecting one's own listening habits
Style features are described with rhythm terms

topics.subject: Musik
topics.name: Copyright and the Music Business
topics.nameDe: Urheberrecht, GEMA und Streaming: Musik als Ware
topics.description: Understand who earns money from music: copyright and performing rights (GEMA in Germany), labels, streaming payouts and platform terms, and what is allowed when downloading, sampling or uploading music and videos.
evidence: Explain what copyright protects and that it expires after a fixed period
Describe how money from a stream is split between artists, labels and the collecting society
Decide whether a given upload (cover, sample, remix) needs permission
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} wants to post a video with a chart song, can they explain whether that is allowed and who holds the rights?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on the Kl. 3–6 introduction to music, media and copyright

topics.laenderNotes: GEMA is the German collecting society; the legal frame is the German Urheberrechtsgesetz within EU law.

topics.subject: Musik
topics.name: Music of a Non-European Culture
topics.nameDe: Musik einer außereuropäischen Kultur (z. B. Westafrika, Indien)
topics.description: Study one non-European musical culture in depth, e.g. West African drumming, Indian raga, Indonesian gamelan or Arabic maqam: its tone system, rhythm, instruments, forms and social or ritual functions, compared with European music.
evidence: Describe the tone system or rhythmic principle of the chosen music (e.g. polyrhythm, raga, maqam)
Explain the social or ritual function of the music in its culture
Play or sing a short pattern from the tradition and compare it with European music
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} hears West African drumming, can they explain polyrhythm and play one layer of the pattern?

prerequisites.reason: Deepens the overview of music from around the world
Rhythmic analysis tools are needed

topics.laenderNotes: The KMK EPA require knowledge of one non-European musical culture for the Abitur; many Länder return to it in the Oberstufe under globalisation and world music.

topics.subject: Musik
topics.name: Jazz: Roots, Styles and Features
topics.nameDe: Jazz: Blues-Wurzeln, Stile und Stilmittel
topics.description: Explain jazz as a synthesis of African American and European traditions: the blues (12-bar form, blue notes), swing, improvisation and the main styles (New Orleans, Swing, Bebop, Cool Jazz, Jazzrock) with typical line-ups and musicians.
evidence: Describe the 12-bar blues form and the blue notes
Recognise two jazz styles by ear and name their typical features
Explain the social background of jazz in the USA
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} hears a swing big band and a bebop combo, can they tell them apart and explain what changed?

prerequisites.reason: Blues and early rock 'n' roll were met in pop history
Swing and syncopation are central to jazz
The blues scheme is built from chords I, IV and V

externalPrerequisites.subject: Geschichte
externalPrerequisites.concept: slavery and racial segregation in the USA
externalPrerequisites.reason: Explains the social roots of blues and jazz

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern: Kl. 10; Berlin-Brandenburg lists jazz among instrumental music for Kl. 7–10.

topics.subject: Musik
topics.name: Music and Politics
topics.nameDe: Musik und Politik: Protestlied, Propaganda, NS-Musikpolitik
topics.description: Analyse how music is used politically: protest and freedom songs, anthems, propaganda music in dictatorships, the Nazi persecution of 'entartete Musik' and censorship in the GDR, and which musical means make music mobilising or manipulative.
evidence: Analyse the musical and textual means of a protest song
Explain with examples how the Nazi regime used and banned music
Discuss whether instrumental music can carry a political message
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} compares a Nazi march with a 1960s protest song, can they explain how each tries to influence listeners?

prerequisites.reason: Protest songs are part of pop history
Builds on how music creates effects

externalPrerequisites.subject: Geschichte
externalPrerequisites.concept: National Socialist dictatorship: propaganda and persecution
externalPrerequisites.reason: Historical context is needed to judge Nazi music policy

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern makes 'Musik politisch' a Lernbereich of Kl. 11; Berlin-Brandenburg lists 'Musik und Herrschaft, Musik als Protest' for Kl. 7–10.

topics.subject: Musik
topics.name: Music and Technology
topics.nameDe: Musik und Technik: elektronische Klangerzeugung, Sampling, Streaming
topics.description: Explain how technology has changed music since the 20th century: electronic instruments and synthesis, recording and sampling, electronic art music (e.g. Stockhausen, Reich), digital distribution and streaming, and their effects on creativity, the music economy and copyright.
evidence: Explain how a synthesizer or sampler produces or changes sound
Describe a work of electronic art music and a technology-based pop style
Discuss how streaming changes what musicians earn and how music is made
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} hears a track built from samples, can they explain the technique and discuss whether it counts as original work?

prerequisites.reason: Hands-on production experience grounds the discussion
Copyright basics are needed to discuss sampling and streaming

externalPrerequisites.subject: Informatik & Medienbildung
externalPrerequisites.concept: data compression and streaming of media
externalPrerequisites.reason: Explains how audio is compressed and transmitted

topics.subject: Musik
topics.name: Overview of Musical Eras
topics.nameDe: Epochenüberblick der Musikgeschichte
topics.description: Order the main eras of Western music (Middle Ages, Renaissance, Baroque, Classical, Romantic, 20th/21st century) on a timeline with dates, typical genres and composers, and assign listening examples to eras by their style features.
evidence: Put the eras in order with approximate dates
Name one typical genre and one composer for each era
Assign an unknown example to an era and justify it with two features
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} hears a harpsichord concerto and a Romantic symphony, can they place both in their eras and explain why?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on the Kl. 3–6 introduction to composers and eras

externalPrerequisites.subject: Geschichte
externalPrerequisites.concept: chronology of European history from the Middle Ages to the modern era
externalPrerequisites.reason: Historical periods frame the musical eras

topics.subject: Musik
topics.name: Viennese Classicism
topics.nameDe: Wiener Klassik: Haydn, Mozart, Beethoven
topics.description: Describe the Viennese Classical style (balanced phrases, clear harmony, contrast and balance), its main genres (symphony, sonata, string quartet, concerto), the composers' path from court musician to free artist, and Beethoven as a bridge to Romanticism.
evidence: Name style features of Classical music and show them in an example
Explain how Haydn's and Beethoven's working conditions differed
Name the movements of a classical symphony and their usual characters
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} compares Haydn's position at court with Beethoven's in Vienna, can they explain what changed for composers?

prerequisites.reason: Places Classicism in the sequence of eras
Motivic work is a hallmark of the style

externalPrerequisites.subject: Geschichte
externalPrerequisites.concept: Enlightenment and the French Revolution
externalPrerequisites.reason: Explains the ideals and social change behind the era

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern: Kl. 9 (with a Beethoven or Schubert portrait already in Kl. 7).

topics.subject: Musik
topics.name: Romantic Music
topics.nameDe: Musik der Romantik: Lied, Charakterstück, Programmmusik, sinfonische Dichtung
topics.description: Characterise Romantic music: expression of feeling, nature and longing, national styles, the virtuoso, small forms (Lied, character piece) and large forms (programme symphony, symphonic poem), with composers such as Schubert, Robert and Clara Schumann, Chopin, Liszt and Wagner.
evidence: Name typical subjects and forms of Romantic music
Show in an example how harmony, dynamics or orchestration express feeling
Explain the difference between programme music and absolute music
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} hears Smetana's 'Moldau', can they explain how it tells a story and why it is typically Romantic?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on programme music from Kl. 3–6
Romantic style is heard against Classical norms

topics.subject: Musik
topics.name: Baroque Music
topics.nameDe: Musik des Barock: Generalbass, Concerto, Oratorium
topics.description: Describe Baroque music (about 1600–1750): basso continuo (Generalbass), terraced dynamics and the doctrine of affects, the concerto principle (concerto grosso, solo concerto), suite, cantata and oratorio, and the role of court and church, with Bach, Händel and Vivaldi.
evidence: Explain the basso continuo and realise a few figured-bass chords
Show the alternation of tutti and soli in a concerto grosso
Relate a Baroque genre to its function at court or in church
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} hears a Vivaldi concerto, can they show where soloist and tutti alternate and explain what the continuo does?

prerequisites.reason: Places the Baroque in the sequence of eras
Figured bass is built from triads and their inversions

externalPrerequisites.subject: Geschichte
externalPrerequisites.concept: absolutism and court culture
externalPrerequisites.reason: Courtly patronage shaped Baroque genres

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern treats the Baroque in Kl. 10 and returns to figured bass in Mu13 (gA); elsewhere Baroque music often comes earlier, e.g. in Kl. 7–8.

topics.subject: Musik
topics.name: Music 1890–1950: Impressionism to Twelve-Tone
topics.nameDe: Musik 1890–1950: Impressionismus, Expressionismus, Atonalität, Zwölftontechnik
topics.description: Explain how composers broke with major-minor tonality around 1900: Debussy's Impressionism (whole-tone scale, sound colour), Expressionism and free atonality, Schoenberg's twelve-tone technique, and Stravinsky's rhythm and Neoclassicism.
evidence: Describe features of Impressionist music in a listening example
Build a simple twelve-tone row and its inversion
Explain why atonal music sounds unfamiliar and how composers organised it
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} hears Debussy and then Schoenberg, can they describe how each moves away from traditional tonality?

prerequisites.reason: Late Romantic style is the starting point of the break
Atonality is defined against major-minor tonality
Parallels with Impressionist painting

topics.subject: Musik
topics.name: History of Western Vocal Music
topics.nameDe: Entwicklungen der abendländischen Vokalmusik: Kantate, Oper, Kunstlied
topics.description: Trace vocal music through the eras: word-music relations in Baroque cantata and oratorio (affects, musical-rhetorical figures), characterisation in Classical opera, and text interpretation in the Romantic Lied, each in its historical and social setting.
evidence: Analyse word-music relations in a Baroque aria or chorus
Explain how a Classical opera scene characterises its figures
Interpret a Romantic Lied with reference to the poem and the ideas of its time
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} compares a Bach aria with a Schubert song, can they explain how each composer interprets the text?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on word-music analysis
Baroque genres are revisited
Opera forms are already known

topics.subject: Musik
topics.name: Gregorian Chant and Renaissance Polyphony
topics.nameDe: Gregorianik, Kirchentonarten und Vokalpolyphonie der Renaissance
topics.description: Describe Gregorian chant (psalmody, melisma, neumes and square notation, church modes) and Renaissance vocal polyphony (motet, mass, madrigal; cantus firmus and parody technique; imitation and word painting).
evidence: Transcribe a short chant from square notation and name its mode
Explain cantus firmus or parody technique with an example
Describe imitation and word painting in a Renaissance motet or madrigal
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees a chant in square notation, can they transcribe it and say which church mode it uses?

prerequisites.reason: Extends the overview of vocal music
Imitative polyphony is known from the fugue

topics.subject: Musik
topics.name: Development of Instrumental Music
topics.nameDe: Entwicklungen der Instrumentalmusik vom Barock bis zur Romantik
topics.description: Compare instrumental music across eras: Baroque concerto and fugue, Classical sonata and symphony, Romantic piano music between salon and virtuosity, programme and absolute music, and how public concerts and audiences changed.
evidence: Compare a Baroque, a Classical and a Romantic instrumental work in texture, form and harmony
Explain the debate between programme music and absolute music
Describe how the public concert changed the role of music
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} gets three short instrumental excerpts, can they order them by era and justify the order with analysis?

prerequisites.reason: Baroque concerto and fugue are compared
Classical sonata and symphony are compared
Romantic instrumental music is compared

topics.subject: Musik
topics.name: New Music after 1945
topics.nameDe: Neue Musik nach 1945: Serialismus, Aleatorik, Klangflächen, Minimal Music
topics.description: Explain main currents of art music since 1945 (serialism, aleatory and chance with Cage, sound-mass composition with Ligeti and Penderecki, minimal music with Reich and Pärt, current trends), their compositional means and notation, and their links to political and social developments.
evidence: Describe the compositional principle of two currents with examples
Read a graphic or aleatoric score and explain what is fixed and what is free
Take a reasoned position on an aesthetic statement about New Music
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} hears Ligeti's 'Atmosphères' and a piece by Steve Reich, can they explain the different principles behind them?

prerequisites.reason: Continues the break with tonality
Graphic notation returns in New Music

topics.subject: Musik
topics.name: Judging Music: Facts and Values
topics.nameDe: Musik beurteilen: Sach- und Werturteil
topics.description: Distinguish factual statements about music (Sachurteil) from value judgements (Werturteil), judge pieces and performances with criteria such as originality, craft, effect, function and context, and respect differing tastes.
evidence: Sort statements about a song into factual statements and value judgements
Judge a piece or performance with at least three named criteria
Explain why two people can judge the same piece differently
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} says a song is 'bad', can they turn this into a judgement with criteria and separate it from facts about the music?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on reflecting musical preferences
Effect is one criterion of judgement

topics.subject: Musik
topics.name: Comparing Interpretations
topics.nameDe: Interpretationsvergleich
topics.description: Compare different recordings or arrangements of the same work (tempo, dynamics, articulation, instrumentation, historically informed or modern performance) and reach a reasoned judgement on each interpretive approach.
evidence: Describe measurable differences between two recordings, e.g. tempo and instrumentation
Relate the differences to interpretive intentions such as historical performance practice
Write a reasoned evaluation of which interpretation suits the work better
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} hears a Bach piece on harpsichord and on a modern piano, can they compare the recordings and justify which convinces them more?

prerequisites.reason: Judgement criteria are needed
Analysis grounds the comparison

topics.subject: Musik
topics.name: Discussing Texts about Music
topics.nameDe: Erörterung musikbezogener Texte
topics.description: Analyse texts about music such as reviews, composers' statements and aesthetic essays, reconstruct their claims, test them against listening examples and write a reasoned discussion, an Abitur task type in Musik.
evidence: Summarise the main claim and arguments of a text about music
Test a claim of the text against a musical example
Write a reasoned statement agreeing or disagreeing with the author
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} reads a critic's review of a concert, can they check the claims against the recording and argue for their own view?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on judging music
Writing a reasoned statement was practised in Deutsch Kl. 5–6

externalPrerequisites.subject: Deutsch
externalPrerequisites.concept: analysing argumentative non-fiction texts
externalPrerequisites.reason: Reconstructing the author's argument needs text-analysis skills

topics.subject: Musik
topics.name: Music Aesthetics
topics.nameDe: Musikästhetik: Ausdrucksästhetik und absolute Musik
topics.description: Discuss basic positions of music aesthetics: music as expression of feeling versus 'tönend bewegte Formen' (Hanslick), autonomy versus function, beauty and the concept of the work, and what music psychology says about why music moves us.
evidence: Explain Hanslick's position and an expression-aesthetic position
Apply one position to a piece they know
Discuss findings of music psychology on music and emotion
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} reads Hanslick's claim that music expresses only itself, can they test it on a film score and on a Bach fugue?

prerequisites.reason: Aesthetic positions are met through texts
The debate arose in the Romantic era

topics.laenderNotes: Leistungskurs topic in most Länder; the KMK EPA name music-aesthetic and music-psychological questions as Leistungskurs extension.

topics.subject: Kunst
topics.name: Parallel Projection
topics.nameDe: Parallelperspektive (Kavalier- und Militärperspektive)
topics.description: Draw objects and nested forms in parallel projection, where receding edges stay parallel, in cavalier or military view, and compare this way of showing space with how objects actually appear and with medieval and East Asian pictures.
evidence: Draw a box and a group of overlapping boxes in cavalier perspective
Explain why parallel edges stay parallel in this projection
Use parallel perspective for an imagined building or machine
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} draws a stack of boxes, can they keep all receding edges parallel and the depth consistent?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on showing near and far through overlap
Oblique drawings of cuboids were introduced in Mathematik Kl. 5

topics.subject: Kunst
topics.name: Two-Point Perspective and Viewpoint
topics.nameDe: Zentralperspektive mit zwei Fluchtpunkten, Horizont und Standpunkt
topics.description: Construct buildings and interiors in two-point perspective, place horizon and vanishing points deliberately, and show how frog's-eye, normal and bird's-eye views change the effect of a picture.
evidence: Construct a building corner in two-point perspective on a given horizon
Change the horizon height and explain the effect of frog's- and bird's-eye view
Find horizon and vanishing points in a photograph or painting
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} draws a street corner, can they place both vanishing points on the horizon and make all edges run towards them?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on one-point perspective from Kl. 5–6
Comparison with parallel projection

topics.subject: Kunst
topics.name: Modelling Form with Light and Shadow
topics.nameDe: Licht-Schatten-Modellierung: Eigenschatten, Schlagschatten, Glanzlicht
topics.description: Make objects look three-dimensional by drawing light and shade from a defined light source (core shadow, cast shadow, reflected light, highlight) with hatching, cross-hatching and tonal steps, and render surfaces and materials.
evidence: Draw a sphere or cylinder with a consistent light source, core and cast shadow
Produce a tonal scale from white to black with pencil or hatching
Render a still-life object so that its material (glass, metal, cloth) can be recognised
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} draws an egg lit from the left, can they put the cast shadow and the highlight in the right places?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on hatching and tonal contrast
Needs careful drawing from observation

topics.subject: Kunst
topics.name: Human Proportion and Figure Drawing
topics.nameDe: Menschliche Figur: Proportionen, Haltung und Bewegung
topics.description: Draw the human figure standing and in movement using proportion schemes (head units, canon), quick gesture drawing and foreshortening, and compare ideals of proportion and beauty from antiquity to today.
evidence: Draw a standing figure with the head-unit proportion scheme
Capture a moving pose in quick gesture sketches
Compare two historical proportion ideals and their effect
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} draws a classmate sitting, can they keep the proportions of head, torso and legs believable?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on portrait drawing
Figure drawing is drawing from observation
Knowing skeleton and joints helps to draw poses

topics.subject: Kunst
topics.name: Itten's Colour Contrasts
topics.nameDe: Farbkontraste nach Itten
topics.description: Recognise and use Itten's seven colour contrasts (hue, light-dark, warm-cold, complementary, simultaneous, saturation, extension) in their own paintings and in artworks, and describe their effect.
evidence: Paint small studies that show at least four of the contrasts
Name the dominant contrast in an artwork and describe its effect
Choose a contrast deliberately for an intended mood
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} looks at a painting by Franz Marc, can they name the main colour contrast and explain what it does?

prerequisites.reason: The colour wheel underlies all contrasts
Warm-cold is one of the contrasts

topics.subject: Kunst
topics.name: Painting Techniques and Paint Application
topics.nameDe: Maltechniken und Farbauftrag: Aquarell, Acryl, Lasur, Pastos
topics.description: Work with different paints (watercolour, gouache, acrylic; in theory also tempera, fresco and oil), apply paint as glaze or impasto, wet-in-wet or dry, and judge how the technique changes expression.
evidence: Produce test fields with glaze, impasto, wet-in-wet and dry-brush application
Choose a technique for a picture and justify it
Describe the paint handling in an artwork, e.g. visible brushwork in van Gogh
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} paints a sky, can they decide between a watercolour glaze and thick acrylic and explain the different effect?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on painting with the school paint box
Tints and shades are used in all techniques

topics.subject: Kunst
topics.name: Additive and Subtractive Colour Mixing
topics.nameDe: Additive und subtraktive Farbmischung
topics.description: Distinguish mixing light (additive: red, green and blue make white, as on screens) from mixing pigments (subtractive: cyan, magenta and yellow make dark, as in printing and painting), and apply this to screens, printing (CMYK) and photography.
evidence: Explain why RGB light mixes to white and CMY pigments mix to dark
Predict mixtures in both systems
Relate the two systems to screens and to four-colour printing
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees that red and green light make yellow on a screen, can they explain why red and green paint do not?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on primary and secondary colours
Light and seeing were treated in Kl. 6 science

externalPrerequisites.subject: Physik
externalPrerequisites.concept: dispersion of white light into the colour spectrum
externalPrerequisites.reason: The spectrum explains additive mixing

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern: subtractive mixing in Kl. 7, additive and subtractive together in Kl. 10.

topics.subject: Kunst
topics.name: Functions of Colour
topics.nameDe: Farbfunktionen: Lokal-, Erscheinungs-, Ausdrucks- und Symbolfarbe
topics.description: Analyse how artists use colour: local colour (an object's own colour), apparent colour (changed by light, as in Impressionism), expressive colour (as in Expressionism) and symbolic colour (as in medieval painting), and use them deliberately.
evidence: Identify the dominant colour function in three artworks
Paint the same motif once in apparent and once in expressive colour
Explain why a colour can carry different symbolic meanings in different cultures
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} compares a Monet and a Kirchner, can they explain the difference between apparent and expressive colour?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on colour contrasts
Colour effect is the basis of expressive colour

topics.subject: Kunst
topics.name: Sculptural Means: Mass, Volume and Space
topics.nameDe: Plastische Gestaltungsmittel: Masse, Volumen, Körper-Raum-Bezug
topics.description: Shape three-dimensional work deliberately with mass, volume, openings, proportion and the relation between body and surrounding space, by adding (modelling, assembling) and removing material, and describe these means in sculptures.
evidence: Build a sculpture that combines closed mass and openings
Explain body-space relation and changing viewpoints in a sculpture
Use balance, joints and supports so that a construction stands
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} builds a figure from wire and plaster, can they explain how the openings change the effect compared with a closed block?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on modelling and carving in Kl. 3–6

topics.subject: Kunst
topics.name: Object Art and the Readymade
topics.nameDe: Objektkunst: Readymade, Objet trouvé, Assemblage, Installation
topics.description: Explain how artists since Duchamp turn everyday objects into art (readymade, objet trouvé, assemblage, installation), how taking objects out of context changes their meaning, and how design objects combine practical, aesthetic and symbolic functions; create an object-based work.
evidence: Explain the idea of the readymade with Duchamp's 'Fountain'
Analyse an object or installation by form, material, function and context
Create a work that changes the meaning of an everyday object and explain the strategy
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees a bicycle wheel on a stool in a museum, can they explain why it can count as art?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on sculptural means
Assemblage extends collage into space

topics.subject: Kunst
topics.name: Intaglio Printing: Drypoint and Etching
topics.nameDe: Tiefdruck: Kaltnadel und Radierung; Druckverfahren im Vergleich
topics.description: Make an intaglio print (drypoint or etching), understand that the ink sits in the grooves, and compare intaglio with relief, planographic and screen printing and with digital reproduction.
evidence: Prepare a plate, ink, wipe and print a small edition of a drypoint
Explain the difference between relief, intaglio, planographic and screen printing
Recognise the technique of a historical print (e.g. Dürer, Rembrandt) from its line quality
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} compares a linocut and a drypoint, can they explain where the ink sits in each and how that shows in the line?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on the relief print
Tone in intaglio is built with lines

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern compares relief, intaglio and screen printing already in Kl. 7; Berlin-Brandenburg names etching for Kl. 9/10.

topics.subject: Kunst
topics.name: Collage and Photomontage
topics.nameDe: Collage und Fotomontage als Gestaltungsprinzip
topics.description: Use collage and montage as a way of thinking: combine found images, text and material to create new meanings, and analyse collage and photomontage in art (Cubism, Dada, John Heartfield, Hannah Höch) and in advertising.
evidence: Create a photomontage that produces a new meaning from combined images
Explain the principle of montage with a Dada or Heartfield example
Analyse how a digital montage in advertising steers the viewer
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees one of John Heartfield's montages of Hitler, can they explain how the combination of images creates the political message?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on collage from the Grundschule
Digital tools are used for montage

topics.subject: Kunst
topics.name: Structured Artwork Analysis
topics.nameDe: Werkanalyse in Schritten: Eindruck, Beschreibung, Analyse, Deutung
topics.description: Analyse an artwork in set steps: first impression, factual data and description, analysis of composition, colour and form, interpretation in context and a reasoned judgement. This is the standard method of Bildanalyse in German art lessons.
evidence: Write a factual description of an artwork moving from the whole to the details
Analyse composition, colour and form with technical terms
Write an interpretation that connects the analysis with the context
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} gets an unknown painting, can they describe it in order, analyse its means and suggest a reasoned interpretation?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on describing artworks
Builds on first interpretation and judgement

externalPrerequisites.subject: Deutsch
externalPrerequisites.concept: writing a factual description of a picture
externalPrerequisites.reason: The writing conventions of description are shared with Deutsch

topics.subject: Kunst
topics.name: Iconography: Reading Subjects and Symbols
topics.nameDe: Ikonografie: christliche und weltliche Bildmotive, Attribute
topics.description: Identify common picture subjects (Annunciation, Nativity, Last Supper, Crucifixion, Pietà; portrait, still life, vanitas) and read attributes, colours and symbols to decode what an image tells.
evidence: Name the subject of a religious painting from its figures and attributes
Explain three vanitas symbols in a still life
Use an iconographic reference work to identify an unknown attribute
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees a woman with a book and a lily and an angel, can they say which scene it is and how they know?

prerequisites.reason: Careful description comes first
Knowing biblical stories helps to read religious images

topics.subject: Kunst
topics.name: Analysing Composition with Sketches
topics.nameDe: Kompositionsskizze: Bildaufbau, Blickachsen, Farbauszug
topics.description: Analyse the structure of a picture with analytical sketches (compositional lines, axes and directions, golden section, figure and ground, colour extracts, light-dark pattern) and explain how they guide the viewer's eye.
evidence: Draw a compositional sketch that shows the main lines and axes
Make a colour or tonal extract of a painting
Explain how the composition guides the viewer's gaze
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} analyses Caspar David Friedrich's 'Wanderer above the Sea of Fog', can they sketch the main axes and explain where the eye is led?

prerequisites.reason: Sketch-based analysis extends the analysis method
Point, line and plane are the analysis terms

topics.subject: Kunst
topics.name: Comparing Artworks
topics.nameDe: Werkvergleich
topics.description: Compare two artworks, e.g. the same subject in two eras, by criteria such as composition, colour, technique, function and context, and draw conclusions about changing views of the world and of art.
evidence: Set up comparison criteria and apply them to two works
Present similarities and differences in a structured text or table
Explain differences with the works' historical contexts
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} compares a medieval and a Renaissance Madonna, can they show how the depiction of space and figure changed and why?

prerequisites.reason: Each work is analysed first
Knowledge of eras explains differences

topics.subject: Kunst
topics.name: Visual Language and the Functions of Images
topics.nameDe: Bildsprache, Bildwirkung und Bildfunktion
topics.description: Explain how the elements of visual language (form, colour, space, composition, technique) together produce meaning and effect, and how images serve functions such as depicting, expressing, persuading or documenting. This is the basis of Werkanalyse at Abitur level.
evidence: Explain how several design means work together in one image to create a meaning
Classify images by their function and justify the classification
Write an analysis that links each observation to its effect
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} analyses a political poster and an Expressionist painting, can they explain how the same means, such as strong colour and distortion, serve different functions?

prerequisites.reason: Composition analysis is a core element
Colour functions are part of visual language

topics.subject: Kunst
topics.name: Iconological Interpretation after Panofsky
topics.nameDe: Ikonografisch-ikonologische Interpretation nach Panofsky
topics.description: Interpret artworks in Panofsky's three stages (pre-iconographic description, iconographic analysis of subject and symbols, iconological interpretation of the work as an expression of its age) and compare the method with others such as formal analysis or reception aesthetics.
evidence: Apply the three stages to a Renaissance or Baroque painting
Explain which sources are needed at the iconographic stage
Compare the iconological method with another method of analysis
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} interprets Holbein's 'The Ambassadors', can they move from what is shown to what the objects meant and to what the painting says about its time?

prerequisites.reason: The iconographic stage builds on reading symbols
Builds on structured analysis

topics.subject: Kunst
topics.name: The Body in Modern and Contemporary Art
topics.nameDe: Körperbilder in der Kunst des 20. und 21. Jahrhunderts
topics.description: Analyse how artists of the 20th and 21st centuries present the human body (figuration, deformation, fragment, the body as material in performance, digital bodies) and relate the works to ideals of beauty, gender and identity.
evidence: Compare two artistic positions on the body with analysis and context
Explain how a work questions ideals of beauty or gender
Develop an own work on body and self-image
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} compares a sculpture by Giacometti with a self-staging by Cindy Sherman, can they explain the different views of the body?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on figure drawing and proportion ideals
Positions after 1945 are needed

topics.subject: Kunst
topics.name: Theories of Art
topics.nameDe: Kunsttheorie: Mimesis, Ausdruck, Autonomie, Institution
topics.description: Discuss theories of what art is and does (imitation or mimesis, expression, autonomy of the image, institutional theory, the expanded concept of art) and apply them to works that challenge the concept of art.
evidence: Explain three theories of art with an example each
Apply a theory to judge whether a controversial work is art
Analyse an artist's statement about art and take a position
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} reads an artist's manifesto, can they place it among theories of art and test it on one of the artist's works?

prerequisites.reason: Theory builds on analysis
Readymades challenge the concept of art

topics.laenderNotes: Leistungskurs content; the KMK EPA name art-theoretical approaches as part of the Leistungskurs.

topics.subject: Kunst
topics.name: Romanesque and Gothic Art
topics.nameDe: Kunst der Romanik und Gotik
topics.description: Describe medieval art (Romanesque and Gothic architecture, sculpture, book illumination and panel painting), its symbolic rather than naturalistic way of showing space, scale by importance and gold ground, and its religious function.
evidence: Name features of Romanesque and Gothic art and assign examples
Explain scale by importance (Bedeutungsperspektive) and gold ground
Describe the religious function of a medieval artwork
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees a medieval altarpiece with a large Mary and tiny donors, can they explain why the figures differ in size?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on the overview of art across the ages
Medieval life in monastery and castle was treated in Geschichte Kl. 6

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern teaches art history chronologically (Kl. 7 Middle Ages to Kl. 11 classical modernism); NRW Sek I is organised by design problems, and Berlin-Brandenburg by themes, so periods come in a free order there.

topics.subject: Kunst
topics.name: Renaissance Art
topics.nameDe: Kunst der Renaissance: Zentralperspektive, Anatomie, neues Menschenbild
topics.description: Explain the Renaissance as a rebirth of antiquity and a human-centred view of the world: central perspective, anatomy and proportion, the picture as a window, new genres such as portrait and landscape, and artists such as Leonardo, Raphael, Michelangelo and Dürer.
evidence: Compare the depiction of space in a medieval and a Renaissance painting
Explain how humanism changed the image of the human being in art
Name three Renaissance artists and a key work by each
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} looks at Leonardo's 'Last Supper', can they find the vanishing point and explain why it lies at Jesus' head?

prerequisites.reason: The Renaissance is understood in contrast to medieval art
Central perspective is the key innovation

externalPrerequisites.subject: Geschichte
externalPrerequisites.concept: Renaissance and humanism
externalPrerequisites.reason: Historical context of the new world view

topics.subject: Kunst
topics.name: Baroque Art
topics.nameDe: Kunst des Barock: Bewegung, Licht, Pathos, Repräsentation
topics.description: Characterise Baroque painting, sculpture and architecture: dynamic diagonal composition, dramatic light (chiaroscuro), pathos and illusion, and art as display of power by the church and absolutist rulers (Bernini, Caravaggio, Rubens, Rembrandt).
evidence: Compare a Renaissance and a Baroque work in composition and movement
Explain chiaroscuro with a Caravaggio or Rembrandt example
Describe how a Baroque palace or church displays power
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} compares Michelangelo's and Bernini's David, can they explain what makes Bernini's version Baroque?

prerequisites.reason: Baroque is defined in relation to the Renaissance

externalPrerequisites.subject: Geschichte
externalPrerequisites.concept: absolutism and court culture
externalPrerequisites.reason: Explains art as a display of power

topics.subject: Kunst
topics.name: Neoclassicism, Romanticism and Realism
topics.nameDe: Klassizismus, Romantik und Realismus
topics.description: Compare three currents of 19th-century art: Neoclassicism (David: clarity, antiquity, revolutionary pathos), Romanticism (Friedrich: feeling, nature, the sublime) and Realism (Courbet, Menzel: social reality), and relate them to revolution, nation and industrialisation.
evidence: Assign three works to the three currents and justify it with features
Explain how a Romantic painting expresses feeling and the sublime
Relate a Realist work to the social conditions of its time
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} compares a painting by David with one by Caspar David Friedrich, can they explain the opposite attitudes behind them?

prerequisites.reason: The sequence of styles continues
Works are analysed with the standard method

externalPrerequisites.subject: Geschichte
externalPrerequisites.concept: French Revolution, nation-building and industrialisation in the 19th century
externalPrerequisites.reason: Historical context for the three currents

topics.subject: Kunst
topics.name: Impressionism and the Pioneers of Modernism
topics.nameDe: Impressionismus und Wegbereiter der Moderne
topics.description: Explain how the Impressionists (Monet, Renoir, Morisot; Manet) painted light and the fleeting moment outdoors, influenced by photography and Japanese prints, and how van Gogh, Cézanne and Gauguin opened the way to modern art.
evidence: Describe Impressionist features: broken brushstroke, apparent colour, everyday subjects
Explain the influence of photography or Japanese woodcuts on the movement
Explain how van Gogh, Cézanne or Gauguin each prepared a modern movement
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} looks at Monet's series of Rouen Cathedral, can they explain why he painted the same building again and again?

prerequisites.reason: Impressionism reacts to academic and Realist painting
Apparent colour is the key Impressionist idea

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern: Kl. 10. NRW has no fixed sequence of periods in Sek I; artists for the Abitur are set in the Zentralabitur Vorgaben.

topics.subject: Kunst
topics.name: Classical Modernism 1900–1945
topics.nameDe: Klassische Moderne: Expressionismus, Kubismus, Futurismus, Abstraktion, Surrealismus
topics.description: Compare the main movements of classical modernism (Expressionism with Brücke and Blauer Reiter, Fauvism, Cubism, Futurism, abstraction, Dada, Surrealism, Neue Sachlichkeit) by their visual language and strategies, including the influence of non-European art.
evidence: Assign works to movements and justify it with visual features
Explain multiple perspectives in Cubism with an example
Discuss the role of non-European art for modernism between inspiration and appropriation
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} compares a Picasso of 1910 with a Kandinsky of 1913, can they explain the two different ways of leaving naturalism behind?

prerequisites.reason: The pioneers of modernism lead into these movements
Der Blaue Reiter was met in the Grundschule

topics.subject: Kunst
topics.name: Art under National Socialism
topics.nameDe: Kunst im Nationalsozialismus: 'Entartete Kunst' und Propaganda
topics.description: Explain how the Nazi regime defamed modern art as 'entartet' (exhibition of 1937), persecuted artists and promoted propagandistic art and architecture, how ideology distorts aesthetic judgement, and why provenance research and restitution of looted art matter.
evidence: Describe the 1937 'Entartete Kunst' exhibition and its aims
Compare a defamed modern work with an officially promoted Nazi work
Explain why provenance research and restitution matter today
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees a painting by Otto Dix that was shown in 'Entartete Kunst', can they explain why the Nazis attacked it?

prerequisites.reason: The defamed art is classical modernism

externalPrerequisites.subject: Geschichte
externalPrerequisites.concept: National Socialist dictatorship: ideology and propaganda
externalPrerequisites.reason: Historical context is essential

topics.subject: Kunst
topics.name: Art after 1945
topics.nameDe: Kunst nach 1945: Informel, Pop Art, Minimal Art, Konzeptkunst
topics.description: Describe key positions of art after 1945 (Abstract Expressionism and Informel, Pop Art, Minimal and Concept Art, Fluxus and Beuys, art in East and West Germany) and their strategies, such as seriality, everyday objects and the idea over the object.
evidence: Characterise three currents after 1945 with examples
Explain Pop Art's use of mass media and seriality
Compare an art position from the GDR with one from the Federal Republic
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees Warhol's Campbell's Soup Cans, can they explain what makes them Pop Art and what they say about consumer society?

prerequisites.reason: Post-war art continues and breaks with modernism

topics.laenderNotes: Which contemporary positions are studied is often fixed by the Länder's Abitur Vorgaben (e.g. NRW Zentralabitur) and changes from year to year.

topics.subject: Kunst
topics.name: Global Art, Canon and Restitution
topics.nameDe: Kunst global: Kanonkritik, kulturelle Aneignung, Raubkunst und Restitution
topics.description: Discuss current debates in the art world (the Eurocentric canon, postcolonial critique, cultural appropriation, the return of looted objects such as the Benin Bronzes, the role of museums) and form a reasoned position.
evidence: Explain the main arguments of the restitution debate with a case
Analyse how a museum presents non-European objects
Take a reasoned position on a case of cultural appropriation
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} reads about the Benin Bronzes in German museums, can they lay out the arguments and justify their own view?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on contemporary positions
Nazi-looted art is an earlier restitution case

externalPrerequisites.subject: Geschichte
externalPrerequisites.concept: European colonialism and imperialism
externalPrerequisites.reason: Colonial history explains how the objects came to Europe

topics.subject: Kunst
topics.name: Building Romanesque and Gothic Churches
topics.nameDe: Sakralbau: Rund- und Spitzbogen, Gewölbe; Kirche, Synagoge, Moschee
topics.description: Explain how Romanesque and Gothic churches are built (round and pointed arch, barrel and rib vault, buttresses, massive and skeleton construction), name the parts of a church, and compare a church with a synagogue and a mosque.
evidence: Explain with a model or sketch why the pointed arch allows higher, lighter walls
Label nave, aisles, transept, apse and choir on a church plan
Compare orientation, layout and symbols of a church, a synagogue and a mosque
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} visits a Gothic cathedral, can they explain how the flying buttresses make the large windows possible?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on building and constructing in the Grundschule
Places of worship were introduced in Religion/Ethik

externalPrerequisites.subject: Physik
externalPrerequisites.concept: forces, equilibrium and stability of structures
externalPrerequisites.reason: Explains why arches and buttresses carry loads

topics.subject: Kunst
topics.name: Architectural Drawing and Model Building
topics.nameDe: Grundriss, Schnitt, Ansicht und Modellbau
topics.description: Read and draw architectural plans (floor plan, section, elevation) to scale and build a model of a room or stage set, considering proportion, light, material and how people will use and move through it.
evidence: Draw a floor plan and an elevation of a room to scale
Build a scale model from card, foam board or wood
Explain how light and proportion in the design serve the users
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} designs a youth room, can they draw it as plan and section to scale and build a model from it?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on building and constructing
Spatial drawing helps to read plans
Scale drawing needs the Mathematik concept of scale

topics.subject: Kunst
topics.name: Urban Planning and the City
topics.nameDe: Städtebau: Idealstadt, Gartenstadt, funktionale Stadt, Smart City
topics.description: Explore a place in their town with sketches and photographs and compare concepts of the city (ideal city, grid city, garden city, functional city, utopias, informal settlements) by aesthetic, social, ecological and functional criteria.
evidence: Document a square or street with urban sketches and photographs
Compare two concepts of the city by criteria
Develop and justify a design proposal for a local place
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} studies their town square, can they suggest a redesign and justify it with criteria such as quality of life and ecology?

prerequisites.reason: Plans and models are the tools of urban design

externalPrerequisites.subject: Erdkunde
externalPrerequisites.concept: urbanisation and models of urban structure
externalPrerequisites.reason: Geography supplies models of urban development

topics.subject: Kunst
topics.name: Modern and Contemporary Architecture
topics.nameDe: Architektur der Moderne und Gegenwart
topics.description: Analyse buildings of the 20th and 21st centuries (Bauhaus, Le Corbusier, Mies van der Rohe, organic and deconstructivist architecture, sustainable building) by form, function, construction, material and symbolism, and discuss current debates such as reconstruction and ecological building.
evidence: Analyse a modern building by form, function, construction and material
Explain 'form follows function' and a counter-position
Develop and justify a design solution for a building task
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} compares the Bauhaus building in Dessau with a deconstructivist museum, can they explain the different ideas of architecture?

prerequisites.reason: Architecture is analysed in plans and models
Bauhaus was met in Kl. 5–6

topics.subject: Kunst
topics.name: Communication Design: Logo, Poster, Typography
topics.nameDe: Kommunikationsdesign: Logo, Plakat, Typografie
topics.description: Design logos, posters and lettering for real or imagined occasions with the criteria of communication design (clarity, distinctiveness, memorability, reproducibility) and the expressive qualities of typefaces, and analyse examples of corporate design.
evidence: Design a logo that meets named criteria and explain it
Lay out a poster with a clear hierarchy of image and text
Analyse how a brand's corporate design communicates its message
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} designs a poster for the school concert, can they explain their choice of typeface, colours and layout?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on lettering and posters from Kl. 3–6

topics.subject: Kunst
topics.name: Photographic Means
topics.nameDe: Fotografische Gestaltungsmittel: Standpunkt, Brennweite, Blende, Belichtungszeit
topics.description: Use the technical and design means of photography deliberately (viewpoint and perspective, framing, focal length, aperture and depth of field, shutter speed, light) and explain their effect in their own and in professional photographs.
evidence: Take photos with shallow and with deep depth of field and explain the settings
Use frog's- and bird's-eye views for a deliberate effect
Analyse the photographic means of a press or advertising photo
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} photographs a classmate, can they blur the background on purpose and explain how they did it?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on framing and perspective

externalPrerequisites.subject: Physik
externalPrerequisites.concept: converging lenses and image formation
externalPrerequisites.reason: Explains focal length and focus

topics.subject: Kunst
topics.name: Self-Staging, Social Media and Image Rights
topics.nameDe: Selbstinszenierung, soziale Medien und Recht am eigenen Bild
topics.description: Stage and photograph themselves in roles, analyse self-presentation in youth cultures and social media (poses, filters, status symbols), and apply the right to one's own image and copyright.
evidence: Create a staged self-portrait series that tries out a role
Analyse the means of self-presentation in influencer images
Explain when a photo of another person may be published
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} wants to post a photo of friends, can they explain whose consent they need and why?

prerequisites.reason: Photographing skills are needed
Builds on the self-portrait
Builds on data-protection basics from Kl. 5–6

topics.laenderNotes: The right to one's own image (Recht am eigenen Bild, KUG) is German law.

topics.subject: Kunst
topics.name: Film Language and Storyboard
topics.nameDe: Filmsprache: Einstellungsgrößen, Perspektive, Montage, Storyboard
topics.description: Use shot sizes, camera angles and movement, editing and sound to tell a short story: plan it with a storyboard, shoot and edit it, and analyse the same means in film and video art.
evidence: Draw a storyboard with shot sizes and angles for a short scene
Film and edit a one-minute clip with at least three shot sizes
Analyse how editing creates tension in a film excerpt
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} plans a short film, can they draw a storyboard and explain why a close-up comes at the key moment?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on stop-motion animation
Framing and perspective carry over to film

externalPrerequisites.subject: Deutsch
externalPrerequisites.concept: film analysis: camera work and editing
externalPrerequisites.reason: Film analysis is also taught in Deutsch

topics.subject: Kunst
topics.name: Photography between Documentation and Staging
topics.nameDe: Fotografie zwischen Dokumentation und Inszenierung
