topics.description: Compare documentary, objective and staged photography in the press, advertising and art, discuss the truth of images and digital manipulation, and produce a documentary or staged series about everyday life.
evidence: Classify photographs as documentary or staged and justify it
Show how editing or cropping can change a photo's message
Produce a photo series and reflect on its claim to truth
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees a famous press photo, can they discuss how far it documents reality and where it may be staged or edited?

prerequisites.reason: Photographic means are needed
Builds on digital editing and manipulation
Recognising manipulated images was introduced in Kl. 5–6

topics.subject: Kunst
topics.name: Product Design and Sustainability
topics.nameDe: Produktdesign: Funktion, Ästhetik, Nachhaltigkeit
topics.description: Evaluate design objects by their practical, aesthetic and symbolic functions, compare craft and industrial production (e.g. Jugendstil and Bauhaus), and consider social and ecological aspects such as resources, durability and repair.
evidence: Analyse a design object by practical, aesthetic and symbolic function
Compare a Jugendstil object with an industrially designed one
Propose a more sustainable design for an everyday product
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} compares two chairs, can they explain which functions each serves and which one is more sustainable?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on Bauhaus and form and function

topics.subject: Kunst
topics.name: Advertising and Persuasive Images
topics.nameDe: Werbung und persuasive Bilder: AIDA, Branding
topics.description: Analyse how advertising and political images persuade (AIDA formula, branding, emotional appeal, image-text relations) in print and digital media, and design a campaign and present it critically.
evidence: Analyse an advert with the AIDA model
Explain how image and text work together in a campaign
Design a poster or post for a cause and reflect on its persuasive means
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} analyses an online ad, can they show how it grabs attention and creates desire, and judge whether it manipulates?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on communication design
Montage is a common persuasive technique

topics.subject: Kunst
topics.name: Developing an Artistic Project
topics.nameDe: Eigenes Gestaltungsvorhaben: von der Idee zum Werk (Skizzenbuch, Portfolio)
topics.description: Develop a self-chosen artistic project from idea to finished work (research, sketchbook or moodboard, trials, decisions and revisions), document it in a portfolio and reflect on the process with reasons.
evidence: Keep a sketchbook or portfolio that shows research, trials and decisions
Explain why they chose material and technique for their intention
Reflect on what worked and what they would change
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} presents a project, can they use their sketchbook to show how the idea developed and justify their decisions?

prerequisites.reason: Reflection uses judging skills
Technique choices draw on known techniques

topics.subject: Kunst
topics.name: Performance and Action Art
topics.nameDe: Performance, Aktionskunst und Happening
topics.description: Understand body, time and space as artistic material in performance, action art and happening, analyse key works (e.g. Beuys, Abramović), and develop and document a short performance of their own.
evidence: Explain what distinguishes a performance from theatre and from a painting
Analyse a performance with regard to body, time, space and audience
Develop, perform and document a short action
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} watches a video of a performance by Marina Abramović, can they explain what makes it art and what role the audience plays?

prerequisites.reason: Interpretation skills transfer to time-based art
Expressive movement from Sport is used

topics.subject: Kunst
topics.name: Studio Task with Written Reflection
topics.nameDe: Gestaltungsaufgabe mit schriftlichem Anteil
topics.description: Solve a set design task in limited time: develop individual image ideas, choose means between depiction and abstraction, realise the work, and explain and reflect on the design decisions in writing, as in the practical Abitur task in Kunst.
evidence: Develop several sketches for a given theme and choose one with reasons
Realise a finished work that fits task and intention
Write a reflection that links decisions to effects
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} gets a practical exam theme such as 'transformation', can they develop an idea, carry it out and explain their choices in writing?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on developing projects independently

topics.laenderNotes: Some Länder examine Kunst mainly in writing (Werkanalyse); a practical task with written part is one of the KMK EPA task types.

topics.subject: Kunst
topics.name: Artistic Intervention and Social Sculpture
topics.nameDe: Künstlerische Intervention und soziale Plastik
topics.description: Explain how contemporary artists intervene in public and social situations (Beuys' social sculpture, participatory and site-specific art, digital interventions) with strategies such as critique, irony or provocation, and plan and document an intervention of their own.
evidence: Explain Beuys' 'social sculpture' and the expanded concept of art
Analyse a participatory work by situation, process and communication
Plan, carry out and document an intervention and reflect on its effect
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} plans an intervention in the school hall, can they explain which strategy they use and what reaction they want?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on performance and action
Beuys and Fluxus belong to post-war art

topics.subject: Kunst
topics.name: Curating an Exhibition
topics.nameDe: Ausstellung konzipieren und präsentieren
topics.description: Plan and realise an exhibition of their own works: choose works, place and form of presentation (room, website, catalogue), write texts, and reflect on the intended effect, also by comparing the concepts of museums and galleries.
evidence: Select and arrange works for a given space according to a concept
Write labels and an introductory text for the exhibition
Compare their concept with a museum exhibition they visited
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}}'s course exhibits its works, can they explain why each piece is placed where it is?

prerequisites.reason: The exhibited works come from studio practice
Museum visits show how exhibitions work

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Sprint Technique and Crouch Start
topics.nameDe: Sprint: Tiefstart, Beschleunigung und Lauf-ABC
topics.description: Sprint 50–100 m with good technique: crouch start on the commands ('Auf die Plätze – Fertig – Los'), acceleration phase, upright running on the balls of the feet with active arm swing, and coordination drills from the Lauf-ABC.
evidence: Perform a crouch start on the starting commands and accelerate smoothly
Sprint with high knees, active foot strike and opposite arm swing
Demonstrate three Lauf-ABC drills and explain what they train
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} runs the 75 m sprint, can they push off powerfully from a crouch start and stay relaxed at top speed?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on sprinting and starts from the Grundschule

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Pacing Middle-Distance Runs
topics.nameDe: Mittel- und Langstreckenlauf: Tempo einteilen (800 m, 1000 m, 12-Minuten-Lauf)
topics.description: Run 800–3000 m or a 12-minute run (Cooper test) at an even, self-chosen pace, use target times per lap, and judge their effort by breathing and heart rate.
evidence: Run a 12-minute run at an even pace and record the distance
Hit planned lap times within a few seconds on a 1000 m run
Explain why starting too fast lowers the overall result
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} runs 1000 m, can they plan their lap times and keep an even pace instead of sprinting the first lap?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on endurance running in Kl. 1–6

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Long Jump Technique
topics.nameDe: Weitsprung: Anlauf, Absprung aus der Zone, Flug und Landung
topics.description: Improve the long jump with a measured, rhythmic run-up, a precise take-off from the zone or board, a stride or hang technique in flight and a far landing, and track their results over time.
evidence: Measure and mark their run-up and hit the take-off zone consistently
Take off upwards from one foot with swinging leg and arms
Land with legs forward and fall forward, and record the improvement over several jumps
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} long-jumps, can they hit the board from their measured run-up and land without falling back?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on jumping from Kl. 1–6
Run-up speed comes from sprinting

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: High Jump: Scissors to Fosbury Flop
topics.nameDe: Hochsprung: Schersprung und Flop
topics.description: Learn the high jump from the scissors jump to the Fosbury flop: curved J-shaped run-up, take-off from the foot away from the bar, back-first bar clearance and safe landing on the mat.
evidence: Run a curved approach and take off from the foot away from the bar
Clear the bar in back layout and land safely on shoulders and back
Measure their run-up and explain why the curve helps
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} does a flop, can they run a curve, take off from the correct foot and cross the bar backwards?

prerequisites.reason: Take-off from one foot is known
Safe landing skills from apparatus gymnastics

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Shot Put
topics.nameDe: Kugelstoßen: Standstoß, Angleiten, Stoß aus dem Ring
topics.description: Put the shot by pushing, not throwing: standing put with full-body extension, then with a preliminary step or glide from the circle within the rules, choosing the technique that suits them.
evidence: Perform a standing put with the shot at the neck and full extension of legs, hip and arm
Add a glide or step and stay in the circle
Explain why the shot must be pushed and what makes a valid attempt
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} puts the shot, can they push it from the neck with a full-body extension and stay in the circle?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on throwing with full-body extension

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern: standing put in Kl. 9, from the circle in Kl. 11; NRW gives shot put as an example of a new discipline in Sek I.

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Silver and Gold Swimming Badges
topics.nameDe: Deutsches Schwimmabzeichen Silber und Gold
topics.description: Meet the requirements of the German swimming badges Silber and Gold: longer swims (20 or 30 minutes, 400 or 800 m), surface diving and underwater swimming, jumps from 3 m, a timed 50 m breaststroke, 25 m front crawl, towing and knowledge of self-rescue.
evidence: Swim 30 minutes and at least 800 m, changing body position without holding on
Dive to about 2 m three times to bring up objects and swim 10 m underwater
Swim 50 m breaststroke in under 1:15 after a racing dive
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} wants the Gold badge, can they swim 30 minutes without stopping and do 50 m breaststroke in under 1:15?

prerequisites.reason: Bronze must be passed first
Front crawl and underwater swimming are part of Gold

topics.laenderNotes: Silber is often reached in Kl. 5–6 and Gold in Kl. 7–8; Bayern asks pupils in Kl. 7 and 8 to meet a badge that matches their ability.

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Competitive Strokes, Starts and Turns
topics.nameDe: Schwimmarten im Wettkampf: Rückenkraul, Delfin, Start und Wende
topics.description: Swim a second and third stroke (back crawl, butterfly basics) in rough form, improve front-crawl breathing, and perform racing starts and turns within the competition rules.
evidence: Swim 50 m back crawl with alternating arms and a steady kick
Perform a racing dive and a legal turn in two strokes
Swim 50 m or 100 m on time and improve their result
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} swims a 50 m race, can they start with a racing dive and turn legally at the wall?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on front crawl
Builds on breaststroke and swimming on the back

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Self-Rescue and Rescue Aids
topics.nameDe: Selbstrettung und Fremdrettung mit Rettungshilfen
topics.description: Know how to help oneself (cramp, cold, currents, ice) and others without endangering oneself: call for help, use rescue aids (pole, ring, ball, rope), push or tow a partner a short distance, and know the risks of a swimming rescue.
evidence: Explain the rescue chain and why rescuing by swimming is dangerous
Throw a ring or rope accurately to a 'casualty' and pull them in
Push or tow a partner 25 m
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees someone struggling in a lake, can they explain what to do first and how to help without swimming out?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on water safety rules
Safe swimming is the precondition

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Lifesaving Badge Bronze
topics.nameDe: Deutsches Rettungsschwimmabzeichen Bronze
topics.description: Learn lifesaving to the level of the German lifesaving badge Bronze (from age 12): swimming in clothes, surface diving, release grips, towing with head, armpit and control holds, landing a casualty and CPR, plus theory on dangers and first aid.
evidence: Swim 100 m in clothes in under 4 minutes and undress in the water
Free themselves from a neck clutch and tow a partner 50 m
Demonstrate landing a casualty and 3 minutes of CPR
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}}'s partner grabs them from behind in the water, can they free themselves and tow the partner to the edge?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on self-rescue and rescue aids
Gold-level swimming skills are needed
First-aid basics support the theory part

topics.laenderNotes: Examined by DLRG, DRK or ASB examiners or qualified teachers. Bayern expects the badge to be largely met in Kl. 10; NRW names Rettungsschwimmen as core content of Bewegungsfeld 4; many schools offer it as a course or AG.

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Lifesaving Badge Silver
topics.nameDe: Deutsches Rettungsschwimmabzeichen Silber
topics.description: Reach the level of the German lifesaving badge Silber (from age 14): 400 m in 15 minutes, 300 m in clothes, 25 m underwater, diving to 3–5 m, timed towing in clothes, handling a rescue device and a combined rescue ending with CPR.
evidence: Swim 400 m in under 15 minutes in three strokes
Tow a clothed partner 50 m in under 4 minutes
Complete the combined rescue exercise from jump to CPR
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} wants to work as a pool assistant, can they complete the combined rescue exercise and explain their duties when giving help?

prerequisites.reason: Bronze is the preceding level

topics.laenderNotes: The KMK EPA name Rettungsschwimmen among the sports of Bewegen im Wasser; Oberstufe swimming courses often include the Silber badge, which is also required for lifeguard jobs and, in most Länder, for teachers who supervise swimming.

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Squat and Straddle Vaults
topics.nameDe: Stützsprünge: Hocke und Grätsche über Bock oder Kasten
topics.description: Vault over buck or box with squat (Hocke) and straddle (Grätsche) from a springboard: rhythmic run-up, two-footed take-off, short hand support, flight and controlled landing, with partners spotting.
evidence: Take off from the springboard with both feet after a rhythmic run-up
Clear the box or buck in squat or straddle with a short hand push
Spot a classmate at the vault with the correct grip
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} vaults over the buck, can they push off with their hands and land steadily while a partner spots?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on jumping, landing and simple vaults
Spotting and safe set-up are required

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Bar Elements: Hip Circle, Swings and Upstart
topics.nameDe: Reck, Stufenbarren und Barren: Hüftumschwung, Schwingen, Kippe
topics.description: Perform basic elements on horizontal bar, uneven bars or parallel bars (backward hip circle, swings, Wende and Kehre, later upstart or hip pull-over) and combine them into a short routine with spotting.
evidence: Perform a backward hip circle on the bar
Swing with body tension on parallel bars or bar and dismount safely
Combine three elements into a routine
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} works on the bar, can they do a backward hip circle and link it with a dismount?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on hanging, supporting and swinging
Linking elements into a routine is known

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern sets some apparatus by gender (parallel bars for boys, uneven bars and beam for girls); most other Länder do not.

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Floor Routine
topics.nameDe: Bodenturnen: Übungsverbindung mit Rollen, Rad, Handstand und Sprüngen
topics.description: Perform a floor routine of at least three linked elements (rolls including a backward roll through high support, cartwheel or round-off, handstand, jumps and turns) fluently and with body tension.
evidence: Link at least three different elements into a fluent floor routine
Perform a backward roll through high support or a round-off
Evaluate a partner's routine with criteria such as fluency and tension
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} presents a floor routine, can they link roll, cartwheel and jump without stopping?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on the Kl. 5–6 routine
Handstand and cartwheel are core elements
Rolls are linked into the routine

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Partner and Group Acrobatics
topics.nameDe: Akrobatik: Partner- und Gruppenpyramiden
topics.description: Build partner balances and group pyramids safely (roles of base, flyer and spotter; safe standing points on hips and shoulders) and present a group composition with acrobatic and gymnastic elements to music.
evidence: Build two partner figures with correct grips and loading points
Take each role (base, flyer, spotter) and explain its task
Present a group composition with build-up and dismount
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}}'s group builds a pyramid, can they say where it is safe to stand on the base and how to dismount with control?

prerequisites.reason: Balance and body tension are needed
Spotting and safety rules

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Handspring Vault
topics.nameDe: Handstützüberschlag am Kasten
topics.description: Perform a handspring over the box from springboard or mini-trampoline: powerful run-up and take-off, quick hand support in handstand position, push-off and landing on the feet, with two spotters.
evidence: Perform the handspring with two spotters and land on the feet
Push off from the hands with an extended body
Spot the handspring with the correct grip
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} does a handspring over the box, can they reach the handstand position on the box and push off to land standing?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on squat and straddle vaults
The handstand position is needed

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Football Technique
topics.nameDe: Fußball: Passen, An- und Mitnahme, Dribbling, Torschuss
topics.description: Use basic football techniques in game-like tasks: inside-foot pass, controlling flat and lifted balls, dribbling with changes of direction and stopping, and shooting on goal.
evidence: Pass accurately with the inside of the foot over 10 m to a moving partner
Control a pass and take it away from a defender in one movement
Dribble through a course with changes of direction and finish with a shot
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} gets the ball under pressure, can they control it with one touch and pass it accurately to a teammate?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on passing, getting open and scoring
Ball control basics

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Football Tactics
topics.nameDe: Fußball: Freilaufen, Doppelpass, Positionsspiel, Standardsituationen
topics.description: Act tactically in football: get open, use give-and-go and overloads in small-sided games, keep positions and running lines, defend man-to-man or in zones and carry out set pieces.
evidence: Create space by getting open and use a give-and-go in a game
Keep their position and shift with the team when possession changes
Carry out a rehearsed set piece such as a corner or free kick
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}}'s team plays 4 against 4, can they move into free space and use a give-and-go to get past a defender?

prerequisites.reason: Tactics need secure technique

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Handball Technique
topics.nameDe: Handball: Passen und Fangen in der Bewegung, Torwurf, Sprungwurf
topics.description: Pass and catch the ball on the move within the step rule, dribble, and shoot at goal from different positions with the overarm throw and, in rough form, the jump shot.
evidence: Pass and catch while running without breaking the step rule
Shoot at goal from different positions with the overarm throw
Perform a jump shot in rough form
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} gets the ball on the wing, can they take three steps, jump and shoot at goal?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on team-game basics
The overarm throw is the basis of the shot

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Handball Tactics
topics.nameDe: Handball: Raumdeckung 6:0/5:1, Tempogegenstoß, Übergeben und Übernehmen
topics.description: Play handball tactically: zone defence (6:0, 5:1) with stepping out and handing over and taking over attackers, fast break after winning the ball, and simple attacking moves with crossings and feints.
evidence: Defend in a 6:0 zone and step out to the player with the ball
Start a fast break immediately after winning the ball
Use a feint or crossing to create a shooting chance
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}}'s team defends in a 6:0 zone, can they step out to the player with the ball and hand over the runner?

prerequisites.reason: Tactics need secure technique

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Basketball Technique
topics.nameDe: Basketball: Dribbling, Stoppen und Sternschritt, Korbleger, Standwurf
topics.description: Use basketball techniques: dribble with changes of direction and hand, stop legally and pivot, pass (chest and bounce pass), and shoot the lay-up and a set shot from close and medium range.
evidence: Dribble with both hands and change direction without travelling
Stop with a jump stop and pivot to protect the ball
Score a lay-up from both sides
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} drives to the basket, can they do a two-step lay-up without travelling?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on team-game basics
Bouncing and catching are needed

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Basketball Tactics
topics.nameDe: Basketball: Give and Go, Fast Break, Block und Abrollen, Mann-Mann-Verteidigung
topics.description: Play basketball tactically: give-and-go, fast break, screens (pick and roll), positional attack in 3 against 3 and man-to-man defence, also in 3x3 as a leisure variant.
evidence: Use a give-and-go or a screen to get open for a shot
Defend their player man-to-man between player and basket
Run a fast break after a defensive rebound
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} plays 3 on 3, can they set a screen for a teammate and roll to the basket?

prerequisites.reason: Tactics need secure technique

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Volleyball Technique
topics.nameDe: Volleyball: oberes und unteres Zuspiel, Aufschlag von unten
topics.description: Play the ball with the overhead pass (Pritschen) and the forearm pass (Baggern), frontally and with a change of direction, serve underhand, and keep rallies going in small-court games.
evidence: Play the overhead pass to a partner ten times in a row
Receive a serve with a forearm pass towards the setter
Serve underhand into the opponent's court
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} receives a serve, can they forearm-pass it high to the setting position?

prerequisites.reason: Net games introduced playing over a net
Ball-handling basics

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Volleyball Tactics
topics.nameDe: Volleyball: Aufschlag von oben, Angriffsschlag, Block, Spielsysteme
topics.description: Play volleyball with three contacts (receive, set, attack), serve overhand, spike and block in rough form, rotate and use simple systems in reduced and full teams, also beach volleyball as a leisure variant.
evidence: Build an attack with three contacts in a game
Serve overhand into the court
Rotate correctly and take their position in a simple system
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}}'s team receives the ball, can they set up an attack with receive, set and spike?

prerequisites.reason: Tactics need secure technique

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Team Games in the Oberstufe: Game Analysis
topics.nameDe: Sportspiele in der Oberstufe: Spielanalyse und taktische Gemeinsamkeiten
topics.description: Deepen technique and individual, group and team tactics in one or more team games, analyse game situations and structures across games (overload, transition, man-to-man and zone defence, field structure), and apply the rules as player and referee, often for the practical exam.
evidence: Apply complex group and team tactics in a game under exam conditions
Analyse a game situation from video with the game's tactical concepts
Explain a tactical principle that several team games share
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} watches a video of their own game, can they explain why an attack failed and which tactical principle would have helped?

prerequisites.reason: Tactics from football
Tactics from handball
Tactics from basketball
Tactics from volleyball

topics.laenderNotes: In NRW each school chooses one team game for continuous progression to the end of Sek I; in the Oberstufe pupils usually specialise in one game for the practical exam.

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Movement Composition with Design Criteria
topics.nameDe: Bewegungsgestaltung nach Gestaltungskriterien: Raum, Zeit, Dynamik
topics.description: Create and present a group composition (gymnastics with hand apparatus, dance or fitness choreography) using design criteria: space (formations, paths, levels), time (counts, tempo, canon, synchrony), dynamics and form, and judge compositions by agreed criteria.
evidence: Plan a group choreography with at least two formation changes and two levels
Perform in time with the music and the group
Judge another group's presentation with agreed criteria
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}}'s group presents a dance, can they explain how they used space and timing and judge another group by the same criteria?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on dance and choreography in Kl. 3–6
Hand apparatus may be used

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern sets dance and hand-apparatus choreography as compulsory for girls only in Kl. 7–10, with fitness gymnastics for all; NRW and Berlin-Brandenburg do not separate by gender.

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Social Dance
topics.nameDe: Gesellschaftstanz: Cha-Cha-Cha, Rock 'n' Roll, Salsa, Discofox
topics.description: Learn a social or ballroom dance with a partner: basic step and rhythm, leading and following, turns and figures, and present a short sequence.
evidence: Dance the basic step in time to the music
Lead or follow a turn with a partner
Present a short sequence of three figures
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} dances Cha-Cha-Cha, can they find the rhythm in the music and dance the basic step with a partner?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on dance from Kl. 3–6
Counting beats and bars in the music

topics.laenderNotes: Social dance is also a Musik topic in Bayern (Kl. 10); many schools add a dance course in Kl. 9–10 outside lessons.

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Choreography in the Oberstufe
topics.nameDe: Bewegungsgestaltung in der Oberstufe: Musikanalyse und Choreografie
topics.description: Analyse a piece of music (counts, beats per minute, sections, breaks), design a choreography for it with given and own elements, rehearse it in a group and present it as a practical exam performance, explaining the design decisions.
evidence: Map the structure of a piece of music in counts and sections
Design and teach a group choreography that follows the musical structure
Explain the design criteria used in the presentation
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}}'s group gets a song, can they count it out, fit the choreography to its sections and explain their choices?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on design criteria
Musical form guides the choreography

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Skiing or Snowboarding at the School Ski Course
topics.nameDe: Ski alpin oder Snowboard im Schulskikurs; FIS-Regeln
topics.description: Glide, brake and turn on skis or a snowboard on easy slopes (snowplough and parallel turns, or side-slipping and linked turns), use the terrain, stop safely, and follow the FIS rules and basic avalanche awareness.
evidence: Stop safely on a slope with snowplough, side-slip or stop turn
Link turns on an easy run with controlled speed
Explain at least five FIS rules
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} skis down an easy run, can they link turns, control their speed and stop safely when someone is in the way?

prerequisites.reason: Balance on rolling and gliding devices is known
Balance skills

topics.laenderNotes: A school ski course (Schulskikurs) in Kl. 7 is typical in Bayern and southern Germany; elsewhere this Bewegungsfeld is covered by inline skating, rowing, canoeing or optional winter trips.

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Judo and Wrestling by the Rules
topics.nameDe: Ringen und Kämpfen: Fallschule, Haltegriffe, Befreiungen, kontrolliertes Werfen
topics.description: Fight with a partner by the rules and fairly: breakfalls backwards, sideways and forwards, hold-downs and escapes on the ground, unbalancing and a simple controlled throw in standing, with rituals of respect.
evidence: Perform breakfalls in three directions after being thrown
Hold a partner down for 10 seconds and escape from a hold
Throw a partner with control and help them land safely
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}}'s partner unbalances them, can they fall safely and then hold the partner down by the rules?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on partner wrestling and judo basics from Kl. 5–6

topics.laenderNotes: NRW excludes striking and kicking from school sport, so combat sports are taught as judo- and wrestling-like forms; Bayern Basissport has no separate combat field.

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Refereeing and Judging Fouls
topics.nameDe: Schieds- und Kampfrichteraufgaben übernehmen
topics.description: Referee games and judge competitions: know the main rules, recognise fouls and their causes (intent, recklessness, lack of skill), use signals and body language, make decisions and accept feedback.
evidence: Referee a school game using the official signals
Explain the reason for a decision to the players
Analyse a foul from a video clip and choose the correct sanction
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} referees a class game and two players clash, can they decide quickly, signal clearly and explain the decision?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on taking roles such as referee in Kl. 5–6
Rules serve fair play

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: First Aid for Sports Injuries
topics.nameDe: Erste Hilfe bei Sportverletzungen (PECH-Regel)
topics.description: Recognise typical sports injuries (sprains, bruises, strains, fractures, concussion) and give first aid: the PECH rule (Pause, Eis, Compression, Hochlagern), recovery position, emergency call, and when play must stop.
evidence: Apply the PECH rule to a sprained ankle
Put a person in the recovery position and make a correct emergency call (112)
Explain why play must stop after a suspected concussion
topics.assessmentPrompt: If a classmate twists an ankle in a game, can {{name}} say what to do in the right order?

prerequisites.reason: Safety awareness in PE
Knowledge of the body

topics.laenderNotes: PECH is the German mnemonic corresponding to RICE.

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Risk and Challenge in Sport
topics.nameDe: Wagnis und Verantwortung: Risiken einschätzen, Angst bewältigen
topics.description: Judge risky sport situations (high jumps, diving, new elements, climbing) by the demand, their own ability and possible dangers, use strategies to cope with fear, adapt the challenge, and decide for or against the risk with reasons.
evidence: Assess a risky task by demand, own ability and danger
Use a strategy against fear, e.g. breaking a task into smaller steps
Explain why they decided to take or refuse a challenge
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} stands on the 3 m board, can they judge whether they are ready and say how they would manage their fear?

prerequisites.reason: Safety knowledge is the basis for judging risk

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Doping in Sport
topics.nameDe: Doping: Formen, Folgen und Ethik
topics.description: Explain what doping is (banned substances and methods such as anabolic steroids, EPO and stimulants), its health risks and why it violates fairness, how anti-doping controls work, and discuss social and political backgrounds such as state doping in the GDR.
evidence: Name three forms of doping and their health risks
Explain why doping is unfair and how controls by WADA and NADA work
Discuss a doping case and the reasons behind it
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} reads about an athlete caught doping, can they explain the health risks and why it is cheating?

prerequisites.reason: Doping is judged by the fair-play principle
Knowledge of the body's response to training

externalPrerequisites.subject: Biologie
externalPrerequisites.concept: hormones and hormonal regulation
externalPrerequisites.reason: Explains how anabolic substances act

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern: Kl. 10, deepened in Sporttheorie (eA); doping is one of the current issues named in the KMK EPA Sport.

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Health Concepts and a Healthy Lifestyle
topics.nameDe: Gesundheit: Risikofaktoren, Salutogenese, gesundheitsorientiertes Training
topics.description: Discuss concepts of health (WHO definition, risk-factor model, Antonovsky's salutogenesis), evaluate the health value of forms of exercise and of nutrition, and derive consequences for lifelong, health-oriented training.
evidence: Compare the risk-factor model with salutogenesis
Assess the health value of a training programme for a given person
Plan a health-oriented weekly activity programme for themselves
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} is asked whether a fitness influencer lives healthily, can they judge it with a health model?

prerequisites.reason: Knowledge of how exercise affects the body
Health-oriented strength training was practised

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Warming Up and Stretching
topics.nameDe: Aufwärmen (allgemein und speziell) und Dehnen
topics.description: Plan and lead a general and a sport-specific warm-up (raising the pulse, mobilising, activating), explain its effects, and perform static and dynamic stretching correctly.
evidence: Lead a 10-minute general warm-up for the class
Add sport-specific exercises for a given sport
Explain why the body should be warm before stretching and intense effort
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} leads the warm-up before a handball lesson, can they plan general and handball-specific parts and explain why?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on warm-up and pulse from Kl. 3–6

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Endurance Training Methods
topics.nameDe: Ausdauertraining: Dauer- und Intervallmethode, Pulskontrolle
topics.description: Train aerobic endurance with the continuous method and the extensive interval method, control intensity by heart rate and breathing, and run, swim or cycle for 25–30 minutes without stopping.
evidence: Exercise aerobically for 25–30 minutes without stopping
Measure their pulse and keep it in a target zone
Explain the difference between the continuous and the interval method
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} wants to get fitter for running, can they explain how the interval method differs from a steady run and how to check the intensity?

prerequisites.reason: Endurance running is the main practice
Pulse and recovery basics
Heart and circulation from Kl. 6 science

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Functional Strength Training
topics.nameDe: Funktionelles Krafttraining und Zirkeltraining
topics.description: Strengthen the major muscle groups (trunk, back, legs, arms) with body-weight and small-equipment exercises and circuit training with correct technique and breathing, and explain health-oriented strength training and muscular balance.
evidence: Perform core and back exercises with correct technique
Set up and run a circuit with stations for different muscle groups
Explain why balanced trunk muscles protect the back
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} does a plank and a squat, can they hold correct posture and explain which muscles they train?

prerequisites.reason: Body and exercise basics
Muscles and skeleton from Kl. 5–6 science
Warm-up comes before strength work

topics.subject: Sport
topics.name: Planning a Personal Training Programme
topics.nameDe: Individuellen Trainingsplan erstellen: Belastungsnormative und Dokumentation
topics.description: Plan, carry out and document a training programme of several weeks for one motor ability using load parameters (intensity, volume, density, duration, frequency), record performances in charts and evaluate the progress.
evidence: Set a training goal and choose method and load parameters for it
Keep a training log and show the progress in a chart
Evaluate the plan after several weeks and adjust it

topics.description: Read a philosophical text methodically: identify thesis, premises, conclusion and key terms, reconstruct the argument in standard form or as a structure diagram, and test it for validity and plausibility.
evidence: Reconstruct an argument from a short text in premise-conclusion form
Draw a structure diagram of a text's line of thought
Check one premise for plausibility and the conclusion for validity
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} reads an excerpt from Plato, can they write the argument down as premises and conclusion?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on building arguments

externalPrerequisites.subject: Deutsch
externalPrerequisites.concept: analysing argumentative non-fiction texts
externalPrerequisites.reason: Shared techniques of text analysis

topics.subject: Religion & Ethik
topics.name: Scepticism and the Limits of Knowledge
topics.nameDe: Skeptizismus: Gorgias, Descartes, Gehirn im Tank
topics.description: Discuss sceptical arguments (Gorgias' three theses, Descartes' methodical doubt, the brain-in-a-vat thought experiment) and answers to them, and their consequences for how we see ourselves and live together.
evidence: Explain Descartes' methodical doubt and the cogito
Use the brain-in-a-vat thought experiment to state the sceptical problem
Discuss whether radical scepticism can be refuted
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} is asked how they know they are not dreaming right now, can they explain Descartes' answer?

prerequisites.reason: Doubt is a starting point of philosophy
Thought experiments are tested as arguments

topics.subject: Religion & Ethik
topics.name: Media Ethics
topics.nameDe: Medienethik: Information und Meinung, Wahrheit, Verantwortung, Daten
topics.description: Distinguish information from opinion, judge the credibility of sources with simple criteria and theories of truth, recognise staged reality and manipulation in social networks, and discuss the responsibility of journalists, platforms and users, including the press code and data protection.
evidence: Separate facts from opinions in a news item
Check a viral claim with criteria of credibility
Discuss who is responsible for a harmful post: author, platform or users
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} sees a shocking post that is shared thousands of times, can they check whether it is true and explain who is responsible?

prerequisites.reason: Recognising false reports was introduced in Kl. 5–6
Media and opinion-forming from Politik Kl. 6
Judging claims needs argument skills

osMatches.note: os focuses on online identity and misinformation

topics.subject: Religion & Ethik
topics.name: Philosophical Problem Reflection
topics.nameDe: Philosophische Problemreflexion: Problemerfassung, -bearbeitung, -verortung
topics.description: Carry out a full philosophical problem reflection on a text, picture or case: identify the problem and place it in context, work on it by analysing and comparing positions, and take and justify a position of one's own. This is the standard structure of Abitur tasks in Philosophie and Ethik.
evidence: Formulate the philosophical problem in a given material
Compare two positions on it with arguments
Write a reasoned own position that weighs the arguments
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} gets an excerpt from Berkeley in the exam, can they state the problem, compare it with another position and take a reasoned stand?

prerequisites.reason: Text analysis is the first step
Dialogical testing of positions

externalPrerequisites.subject: Deutsch
externalPrerequisites.concept: writing an argumentative essay (Erörterung)
externalPrerequisites.reason: Shared conventions of argumentative writing

topics.laenderNotes: The task format is used by Philosophie (e.g. NRW, Berlin, Brandenburg in Sek II), Ethik (e.g. Bayern, Baden-Württemberg, Sachsen) and Werte und Normen (Niedersachsen). Ev./kath. Religionslehre use the related operators of the religion EPA. In G8 Länder such as Berlin and Brandenburg the Oberstufe starts one year earlier.

topics.subject: Religion & Ethik
topics.name: Fallacies and Unfair Argument
topics.nameDe: Fehlschlüsse und unlautere Argumentation
topics.description: Recognise fallacies and unfair techniques (ad hominem, appeal to the majority, straw man, slippery slope, is-ought fallacy) in debates and online, and respond to them fairly.
evidence: Identify three fallacies in a debate transcript or comment thread
Explain why an inference from 'is' to 'ought' is invalid
Rephrase a fallacious argument into a fair one
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} reads 'If we allow this, soon everything will be allowed', can they name the type of argument and test it?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on valid argument

topics.subject: Religion & Ethik
topics.name: Utilitarianism
topics.nameDe: Utilitarismus: Bentham, Mill; Handlungs-, Regel- und Präferenzutilitarismus
topics.description: Explain the utilitarian principle of the greatest happiness of the greatest number, Bentham's hedonic calculus and Mill's higher pleasures, act, rule and preference utilitarianism (Singer), apply them to cases and discuss objections concerning justice and minority rights.
evidence: Apply the utilitarian calculation to a moral dilemma
Explain the difference between act and rule utilitarianism
Discuss an objection, e.g. sacrificing one person for many
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} considers the trolley dilemma, can they explain what a utilitarian would do and why critics object?

prerequisites.reason: Judging actions by their consequences was introduced
Ethical arguments are tested

osMatches.note: os covers consequentialism, deontology and virtue ethics in one topic

topics.laenderNotes: Core Oberstufe content of Ethik and Philosophie in all Länder; ev./kath. RU treat it among models of ethical judgement (Leitfrage 'Was soll ich tun?').

topics.subject: Religion & Ethik
topics.name: Kant's Ethics of Duty
topics.nameDe: Pflichtethik Kants: guter Wille und kategorischer Imperativ
topics.description: Explain Kant's deontological ethics: the good will, acting from duty versus in accordance with duty, the categorical imperative in its formula of universal law and its formula of humanity, and autonomy; test the imperative on cases and against objections.
evidence: Test a maxim with the formula of universal law
Explain the formula of humanity and its link to human dignity
Compare Kant's ethics with utilitarianism on one case
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} wonders whether a lie to protect a friend is allowed, can they test the maxim with the categorical imperative?

prerequisites.reason: Testing maxims requires logical reasoning
The Golden Rule is a precursor

osMatches.note: os covers three frameworks in one topic

topics.subject: Religion & Ethik
topics.name: Aristotle's Virtue Ethics
topics.nameDe: Tugendethik des Aristoteles: Mesoteslehre und Eudaimonie
topics.description: Explain Aristotle's virtue ethics: the good life (eudaimonia) as goal, ethical and intellectual virtues acquired by habit, the doctrine of the mean (courage between cowardice and recklessness) and practical wisdom, and compare it with rule-based ethics.
evidence: Explain the doctrine of the mean with two virtues
Explain why virtues are acquired by practice
Discuss strengths and weaknesses of virtue ethics compared with Kant
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} is asked whether being extremely honest can be a fault, can they answer with Aristotle's doctrine of the mean?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on reflecting happiness
Aristotle's kinds of friendship are known

osMatches.note: os covers three frameworks in one topic

topics.subject: Religion & Ethik
topics.name: Discourse Ethics
topics.nameDe: Diskursethik nach Habermas
topics.description: Explain Habermas' discourse ethics: a norm is valid if all those affected could agree to it in a free, rational discourse; the rules of discourse and the ideal speech situation, their use for solving conflicts, and objections.
evidence: State the discourse principle and two rules of discourse
Apply discourse ethics to a conflict between stakeholders
Discuss an objection, e.g. the problem of those who cannot take part, like future generations
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}}'s school must decide on a mobile-phone ban, can they explain how a discourse-ethical process would reach a fair rule?

prerequisites.reason: Discourse ethics transforms Kant's universalisation

topics.laenderNotes: NRW: Leistungskurs only; Bayern already teaches Habermas at grundlegendem Anforderungsniveau (Eth12).

topics.subject: Religion & Ethik
topics.name: Nietzsche's Critique of Morality
topics.nameDe: Moralkritik Nietzsches: Herren- und Sklavenmoral, Nihilismus
topics.description: Explain Nietzsche's genealogy of morals (master and slave morality, 'herd morality', resentment), his diagnosis of nihilism and his ideal of self-determination, and discuss what follows for the possibility of justifying morality.
evidence: Explain the distinction between master and slave morality
Relate Nietzsche's critique to Christian or Kantian ethics
Assess whether the critique undermines all morality
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} reads Nietzsche on 'herd morality', can they explain his claim and argue whether he is right?

prerequisites.reason: Kant is one target of the critique
Nietzsche's 'death of God' is known

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern: eA plan (Eth12); elsewhere an optional author in the Leistungskurs.

topics.subject: Religion & Ethik
topics.name: Ethical Judgement in Steps
topics.nameDe: Ethische Urteilsbildung: Schritte und Kriterien
topics.description: Form a well-founded moral judgement on a case in steps: describe the situation and those affected, name the conflicting values and norms, apply ethical theories, weigh the arguments and justify a decision. The method is shared by Ethik, Philosophie and ev./kath. Religionslehre.
evidence: Analyse a case with a step model of ethical judgement
Apply at least two ethical theories and compare their results
Write a reasoned judgement that addresses counter-arguments
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} gets a case about organ donation, can they work through the steps and reach a reasoned judgement?

prerequisites.reason: The theories are applied
The theories are applied
Avoiding fallacies

topics.laenderNotes: In ev./kath. RU the step models (e.g. after Tödt) also weigh biblical and theological arguments and church positions.

topics.subject: Religion & Ethik
topics.name: Cultural Relativism and Universalism
topics.nameDe: Werte und Normen zwischen Kulturrelativismus und Universalismus
topics.description: Compare cultural relativism (moral norms are valid only within a culture) with universalist positions (some norms bind all humans), test both on cases such as human rights or traditional practices, and evaluate their consequences for tolerance.
evidence: Explain a culturally relativist and a universalist position in their argumentative steps
Apply both to a concrete case
Judge which position better supports tolerance and human rights
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} hears 'that is just their culture' about a practice that harms children, can they discuss relativism and universalism?

prerequisites.reason: Respect and diversity are the starting point
Positions are reconstructed as arguments

topics.subject: Religion & Ethik
topics.name: Medical Ethics and Assisted Dying
topics.nameDe: Medizinethik: vier Prinzipien und Sterbehilfe
topics.description: Apply the four principles of medical ethics (autonomy, non-maleficence, beneficence, justice) and the concepts of person and moral status to cases, especially assisted dying (passive, indirect and active euthanasia, assisted suicide) in the context of German law.
evidence: Apply the four principles to a medical case
Distinguish forms of assisted dying and the German legal situation
Evaluate an argument such as the slippery-slope argument in the debate
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} discusses whether doctors should help a terminally ill patient to die, can they use the four principles and the different forms of assisted dying?

prerequisites.reason: Medical-ethical arguments are tested
Builds on reflecting death and grief

topics.laenderNotes: The legal frame (Federal Constitutional Court ruling of 2020 on § 217 StGB) is German. In kath. RU the Church's position on the protection of life is a required perspective.

topics.subject: Religion & Ethik
topics.name: Bioethics at the Beginning of Life
topics.nameDe: Bioethik am Lebensanfang: Pränataldiagnostik, PID, Genomeditierung, Schwangerschaftsabbruch
topics.description: Discuss ethical questions at the beginning of life (prenatal and preimplantation diagnosis, genome editing with CRISPR, abortion) using the concepts of person, dignity and moral status of the embryo (the SKIP arguments) and different ethical theories.
evidence: Explain the SKIP arguments for the moral status of the embryo
Compare two positions on preimplantation diagnosis
Take a reasoned position on genome editing of embryos
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} reads about 'designer babies', can they discuss genome editing with the arguments about the moral status of the embryo?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on the four principles
Human dignity is the central concept

externalPrerequisites.subject: Biologie
externalPrerequisites.concept: genetic engineering and genome editing (CRISPR/Cas9)
externalPrerequisites.reason: Scientific basis of the techniques

topics.laenderNotes: Germany's Embryonenschutzgesetz is stricter than the law in many other countries; ev. and kath. RU also discuss the churches' positions.

topics.subject: Religion & Ethik
topics.name: Ethics of Technology and Artificial Intelligence
topics.nameDe: Technik- und KI-Ethik: Verantwortung, Autonomie, Diskriminierung
topics.description: Discuss ethical problems of technology and AI: responsibility for decisions of autonomous systems such as self-driving cars, bias and discrimination in algorithms, surveillance and data, generative AI and authorship, and whether machines can be moral agents.
evidence: Apply two ethical theories to a dilemma of an autonomous car
Explain how bias in training data leads to discrimination
Take a reasoned position on who is responsible for an AI decision
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} hears that an AI tool rejected job applicants unfairly, can they explain how this happens and who is responsible?

prerequisites.reason: Theories are applied
Builds on media and data ethics

externalPrerequisites.subject: Informatik & Medienbildung
externalPrerequisites.concept: how machine-learning systems learn from training data
externalPrerequisites.reason: Technical basis of AI systems

topics.laenderNotes: The new NRW Sek II plan for Philosophie (in force from 2027) makes artificial intelligence a compulsory applied-ethics and epistemology topic.

topics.subject: Religion & Ethik
topics.name: Jonas' Ethics of Responsibility
topics.nameDe: Verantwortungsethik nach Hans Jonas: Fernethik und Heuristik der Furcht
topics.description: Explain Hans Jonas' imperative of responsibility for future generations and for nature (the new categorical imperative, ethics of distance, heuristics of fear), apply it to climate change and technological risks, and discuss intergenerational justice.
evidence: State Jonas' new categorical imperative and how it differs from Kant's
Apply the heuristics of fear to a technological risk
Discuss obligations to future generations in climate policy
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} discusses whether we owe anything to people born in 100 years, can they use Jonas' argument?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on environmental ethics
Jonas reformulates Kant's imperative

topics.subject: Religion & Ethik
topics.name: Human Beings as Natural and Cultural Beings
topics.nameDe: Der Mensch als Natur- und Kulturwesen
topics.description: Discuss what makes humans special: evolutionary origins and behaviour (cooperation, aggression), the human as a 'deficient being' that needs culture (Gehlen), as spirit open to the world (Scheler), language and education, and why any definition of human nature is problematic.
evidence: Explain one anthropological position in its main steps
Compare a biological and a cultural explanation of a behaviour
Discuss why any definition of 'human nature' is problematic
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} hears that aggression is 'just human nature', can they discuss this with biological and cultural arguments?

prerequisites.reason: Anthropological texts are analysed
Identity questions lead to anthropology

externalPrerequisites.subject: Biologie
externalPrerequisites.concept: human evolution
externalPrerequisites.reason: Evolutionary biology informs the debate

topics.subject: Religion & Ethik
topics.name: Human Dignity and Personhood
topics.nameDe: Menschenwürde und Personbegriff
topics.description: Explain what human dignity means and how it is justified (theologically through the image of God, by Kant through persons as ends in themselves, in Art. 1 of the Grundgesetz), and discuss the concept of the person (Locke, Singer) and its ethical consequences.
evidence: Compare a religious and a Kantian justification of human dignity
Explain why Art. 1 GG makes dignity inviolable
Discuss a case in which the concept of person is contested
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} reads Art. 1 of the Grundgesetz, can they explain two ways to justify why human dignity is inviolable?

prerequisites.reason: Basic rights of the Grundgesetz from Politik Kl. 6
Justice and children's rights are known

topics.laenderNotes: In ev./kath. RU the theological justification (Gottebenbildlichkeit) is required; Ethik and Philosophie start from Kant and the Grundgesetz.

topics.subject: Religion & Ethik
topics.name: Free Will and Determinism
topics.nameDe: Willensfreiheit und Determinismus: Libet-Experiment, Kompatibilismus
topics.description: Discuss whether the will is free: determinist and indeterminist positions, findings of neuroscience (Libet experiment, Roth, Singer) and their critique ('reasons are not causes'), compatibilism (Bieri), and the consequences for responsibility and punishment.
evidence: Explain a determinist and an indeterminist position
Explain the Libet experiment and two objections to its interpretation
Discuss what follows for moral responsibility if the will is not free
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} hears that brain research proves we have no free will, can they explain the Libet experiment and why philosophers doubt the conclusion?

prerequisites.reason: Responsibility presupposes some freedom
Images of humanity frame the question

externalPrerequisites.subject: Biologie
externalPrerequisites.concept: structure and function of the brain and nervous system
externalPrerequisites.reason: Neuroscientific findings need biological basics

topics.laenderNotes: NRW: the Grundkurs treats a determinist and an indeterminist position, the Leistungskurs adds compatibilism; Bayern adds Kant, Sartre and Bieri on freedom.

topics.subject: Religion & Ethik
topics.name: Rationalism and Empiricism
topics.nameDe: Erkenntnistheorie: Rationalismus und Empirismus (Descartes, Locke, Hume)
topics.description: Compare rationalist (Descartes: innate ideas, reason as the source of knowledge) and empiricist theories of knowledge (Locke's tabula rasa, Hume's impressions and ideas and the problem of induction), and judge their strengths and weaknesses.
evidence: Reconstruct Descartes' and Locke's views on the origin of knowledge
Explain Hume's problem of induction
Assess which position better explains mathematical and scientific knowledge
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} is asked whether we know that the sun will rise tomorrow, can they explain Hume's problem of induction?

prerequisites.reason: Scepticism raises the question of certain knowledge
Classical texts are analysed

topics.laenderNotes: The KMK EPA Philosophie illustrate an Abitur task with Berkeley's empiricism; Bayern teaches epistemology mainly in the eA plan.

topics.subject: Religion & Ethik
topics.name: Kant's Theory of Knowledge
topics.nameDe: Kants Erkenntnistheorie: a priori, a posteriori, synthetische Urteile
topics.description: Explain Kant's synthesis of rationalism and empiricism: judgements a priori and a posteriori, analytic and synthetic, forms of intuition and categories, the 'Copernican turn' and the limits of knowledge (things in themselves).
evidence: Classify judgements as analytic or synthetic and as a priori or a posteriori
Explain the Copernican turn in Kant's epistemology
Explain why for Kant we cannot know things in themselves
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} is asked whether '7 + 5 = 12' tells us something new, can they explain Kant's idea of synthetic judgements a priori?

prerequisites.reason: Kant mediates between the two positions

topics.subject: Religion & Ethik
topics.name: Philosophy of Science
topics.nameDe: Wissenschaftstheorie: Induktion, Falsifikation (Popper), Paradigmenwechsel (Kuhn)
topics.description: Discuss how science gains knowledge and how far it can be trusted: induction and its problem, Popper's falsificationism, Kuhn's paradigm shifts, criteria that separate science from pseudoscience, and the reliability of knowledge generated by AI.
evidence: Explain Popper's principle of falsification with an example
Apply criteria to decide whether a claim is scientific or pseudoscientific
Discuss how reliable knowledge generated by AI systems is
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} reads that astrology is 'confirmed by experience', can they use Popper's criterion to test the claim?

prerequisites.reason: The problem of induction is known
Recognising pseudoscientific arguments

externalPrerequisites.subject: Physik
externalPrerequisites.concept: the scientific method: hypothesis, experiment and theory
externalPrerequisites.reason: Examples from physics illustrate theory testing

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern: Popper in the eA plan; NRW: validity claims of the sciences in Grund- and Leistungskurs.

topics.subject: Religion & Ethik
topics.name: The Mind–Body Problem
topics.nameDe: Leib-Seele-Problem: Dualismus und Materialismus
topics.description: Compare dualist positions (Descartes, interactionist dualism) and materialist-monist positions (identity theory, functionalism) on how mind and body relate, discuss the problem of consciousness (qualia), and ask whether AI systems could have minds.
evidence: Reconstruct a dualist and a materialist position
Explain the qualia problem with a thought experiment such as Mary's room
Discuss whether a computer could have consciousness
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} asks whether a chatbot really understands, can they discuss it with dualist and materialist positions?

prerequisites.reason: Descartes' philosophy is known
Neuroscience debates link to the mind-body problem

topics.laenderNotes: Compulsory in the NRW Qualifikationsphase; in other Länder philosophy of mind is often an elective topic.

topics.subject: Religion & Ethik
topics.name: Social Contract Theories
topics.nameDe: Staatsphilosophie: Gesellschaftsvertrag bei Hobbes, Locke und Rousseau
topics.description: Explain why state power needs legitimation and how contract theories justify it (Hobbes' state of nature and Leviathan, Locke's natural rights and right of resistance, Rousseau's general will), and assess them in view of democracy and its endangerment by populism.
evidence: Compare the state of nature in Hobbes and Locke
Explain how each theory legitimises state power
Assess a populist claim with the idea of the general will or of rights
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} imagines a world without government, can they explain what Hobbes and Locke would expect and what follows for the state?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on the purpose of rules
Athenian democracy from Geschichte Kl. 6

externalPrerequisites.subject: Politik und Wirtschaft
externalPrerequisites.concept: principles of democracy: popular sovereignty and separation of powers
externalPrerequisites.reason: Political concepts are needed

topics.subject: Religion & Ethik
topics.name: Human Rights: Justification and Universality
topics.nameDe: Menschenrechte: Begründung, universeller Geltungsanspruch und Durchsetzung
topics.description: Explain the justification of human rights (natural law, human dignity, contract), the Universal Declaration of 1948, objections from cultural relativism and problems of enforcement, and develop their own position on universal validity.
evidence: Explain two justifications of human rights
Discuss an objection to their universality
Analyse a case where human rights are violated and how they could be enforced
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} hears that human rights are a Western idea, can they discuss the objection and give a reasoned answer?

prerequisites.reason: Human dignity grounds human rights
The relativism objection is known

topics.subject: Religion & Ethik
topics.name: Theories of Justice: Aristotle and Rawls
topics.nameDe: Gerechtigkeitstheorien: Aristoteles und Rawls
topics.description: Explain Aristotle's distinction between distributive and corrective (commutative) justice and Rawls' justice as fairness (original position, veil of ignorance, two principles, difference principle), and apply them to questions of social justice such as fair wages or equal opportunities in education.
evidence: Distinguish distributive and commutative justice with examples
Explain the veil of ignorance and the difference principle
Apply Rawls to a current question of social justice
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} discusses whether managers should earn 100 times more than workers, can they argue with Rawls' difference principle?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on fairness and justice from the Grundschule
Rawls sets his theory against utilitarianism

osMatches.note: fairness, equality and equity for younger pupils

topics.subject: Religion & Ethik
topics.name: Arendt: Power, Violence and the Banality of Evil
topics.nameDe: Hannah Arendt: Macht und Gewalt; Eichmann-Prozess
topics.description: Explain Hannah Arendt's distinction between power (people acting together) and violence, and her report on the Eichmann trial with the thesis of the 'banality of evil', and discuss the tension between law and justice in the prosecution of Nazi crimes.
evidence: Explain Arendt's distinction between power and violence
Explain the thesis of the banality of evil and the criticism of it
Discuss the Eichmann trial as a case of law and justice
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} reads about Eichmann as a 'desk perpetrator', can they explain what Arendt meant by the banality of evil?

prerequisites.reason: Theories of state power are known
Conscience and obedience

externalPrerequisites.subject: Geschichte
externalPrerequisites.concept: the Holocaust and Nazi crimes
externalPrerequisites.reason: Historical knowledge of the Holocaust is required

topics.subject: Religion & Ethik
topics.name: Religion and Science
topics.nameDe: Religion und Naturwissenschaft: Schöpfung, Evolution und Modelle ihres Verhältnisses
topics.description: Compare models of the relationship between religion and science (conflict, independence, dialogue, integration), read creation texts and the theory of evolution each in their own kind of language, and discuss truth claims, creationism and the limits of scientific explanation.
evidence: Explain two models of the relationship between faith and science
Compare the kind of statement made in Genesis 1 with that of evolution theory
Discuss why creationism is criticised by scientists and theologians alike
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} hears that evolution disproves God, can they explain the different kinds of statements and the models of their relationship?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on creation stories and science
Questions about the limits of knowledge

externalPrerequisites.subject: Biologie
externalPrerequisites.concept: theory of evolution
externalPrerequisites.reason: The scientific theory must be understood

topics.laenderNotes: Core Oberstufe topic of ev./kath. RU (Leitfrage 'Was ist wahr?'); in Ethik and Philosophie it belongs to truth and knowledge.

topics.subject: Religion & Ethik
topics.name: The Question of God
topics.nameDe: Die Gottesfrage: Gottesbilder, Theismus, Atheismus, Agnostizismus
topics.description: Discuss ways of speaking about God (personal God, images and metaphors, negative theology, the Trinity), arguments of theism, atheism and agnosticism, and what believing in God means for a person's life.
evidence: Compare two images of God and their function
Reconstruct an atheist and a theist argument
Explain why many theologians call talk about God analogical or metaphorical
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} says they cannot imagine an old man in the sky, can they explain other ways in which religions speak about God?

prerequisites.reason: Proofs and theodicy were discussed
Critiques of religion are known

topics.laenderNotes: Ev. RU focuses on the Christian talk of God (e.g. Luther, Bonhoeffer), kath. RU adds the teaching of the Church; in Ethik and Philosophie the topic appears as philosophy of religion.

topics.subject: Religion & Ethik
topics.name: Religion and State in Germany
topics.nameDe: Religion und Staat in Deutschland: Religionsfreiheit, Religionsunterricht, Kirchensteuer
topics.description: Explain the German model of state and religion: freedom of religion (Art. 4 GG), religious neutrality combined with cooperation (Art. 7 Abs. 3 GG on religious education, Art. 140 GG on church tax and the legal status of religious communities), positive and negative freedom of religion, and current debates such as crucifix, headscarf and Islamic religious education.
evidence: Explain positive and negative freedom of religion with a case
Describe the legal basis of religious education and of church tax
Discuss a court case such as the crucifix or headscarf ruling
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} wonders why a state school offers religious education, can they explain the constitutional basis and the alternatives?

prerequisites.reason: Basic rights of the Grundgesetz
Muslim life and debates in Germany

externalPrerequisites.subject: Politik und Wirtschaft
externalPrerequisites.concept: the Grundgesetz and the Federal Constitutional Court
externalPrerequisites.reason: Constitutional institutions are needed

topics.laenderNotes: Special arrangements exist in Berlin and Bremen (Art. 141 GG, 'Bremer Klausel'), in Brandenburg (LER as ordinary subject) and in Hamburg ('Religionsunterricht für alle').

topics.subject: Religion & Ethik
topics.name: Interreligious Dialogue and Truth Claims
topics.nameDe: Interreligiöser Dialog: Exklusivismus, Inklusivismus, Pluralismus
topics.description: Compare models of how religions relate to each other's truth claims (exclusivism, inclusivism, pluralism), know criteria for constructive dialogue, and take part in or plan a dialogue encounter.
evidence: Explain the three models with an example each
Name criteria for respectful interreligious dialogue
Plan or reflect on a dialogue encounter, e.g. a visit to a synagogue or mosque
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} hears 'only my religion is true', can they place the statement among the models and discuss how dialogue is still possible?

prerequisites.reason: Knowledge of several religions
Knowledge of Islam
Relativism and universalism relate to pluralism

topics.laenderNotes: Dialogue competence is a required competence of ev. and kath. RU in the KMK EPA; in Ethik interreligious content appears as comparative study of religions.

topics.subject: Religion & Ethik
topics.name: Hope in the Face of Death
topics.nameDe: Was darf ich hoffen? Tod und Jenseitsvorstellungen der Religionen
topics.description: Compare religious and secular answers to death and suffering: resurrection in Christianity, the hereafter in Judaism and Islam, rebirth and liberation in Hinduism and Buddhism, and secular views such as Epicurus', and reflect on what hope means for living.
evidence: Compare the ideas of the hereafter of three religions
Explain a secular position on death, e.g. Epicurus'
Discuss how ideas about death shape how people live
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} is asked what religions say happens after death, can they compare three answers and a secular view?

Rebirth and nirvana are known

evidence: Compare the ideas of happiness of Aristotle, Epicurus and the Stoics
Explain Frankl's idea that meaning is found through self-transcendence
Assess a finding of happiness research for their own life
